Cory just a bit of RE lore, so basically Luis made Nemesis from RE3. He played a really big part in the creation of the NE-alpha parasite which is the main thing that gives Nemesis his power along with the T-virus. The reason Luis knows so much about the plagas parasite (the one infecting everyone in RE4) is because he studied it for Umbrella. The NE-a parasite is a modified version of las plagas which Luis made. Nemesis started off as a tyrant just like Mr. X from RE2 and they injected a tyrant with the NE-a parasite to create the monstrosity we know as the Nemesis. A key bit of info is the Europe Umbrella Team photo in Luis's office and if you look close you can see Luis in the photo. At the beginning of RE3 remake the same Europe team was shown making Nemesis. Cool little detail from Capcom that interconnects all the RE games together.

Atsu and Jubei’s relationship is so complex and I love it.

Anyway, I saw a comment talking about how Atsu was able to forgive Oyuki, the woman who helped in the murder of her family, compared to her brother.

And I don’t think it’s just forgiveness.

With Oyuki: Oyuki like Atsu, was alienated because of her gender, forced to live a life she didn’t want to live, and lost everything to the hands of Saito (Oyuki lost her family when Saito’s Clan lost in a War).

With Jubei: Yes, both went through the trauma of losing their family, however, Jubei, was found by a samurai, nursed back to health, fed, sheltered, and cared for. Atsu, had nothing like that. She had to survive on her own with nothing but swordsmanship and her mother’s shamisen. 

It’s not jealousy, but, I think it’s because of the differences in the way they both grew up, is what’s making Atsu so cold towards her brother. 

It’s like two different sides of the same coin.

On one side, you have Jubei, who, grew up able to move on from his family’s death and revenge, and become a Matsumae General(?) because of the samurai who took him in, fed him, clothed him, and nursed him.

On the other side of the coin, is Atsu. Because of her lack of guidance and companionship, and  nothing but her thoughts, she is now stuck in the past, as we can see when she reminisces on her childhood before Saito killed her family. Unlike Jubei, she had no guardian to take care of her, so she was forced to fend for herself and live by herself.

Basically, it was easier for Atsu to forgive Oyuki, one, they had a common enemy, The Kitsune. Two,  similar trauma and similar backstories, three, they remind me of opposites. And four, because of the relationship they made.

Yes, people can argue that Atsu shared a common enemy with Jubei as well. Lord Saito and The Oni more specifically. And people could also argue that Jubei and Atsu have a relationship as brother and sister. Let me rephrase “had” a relationship. Once their family was slaughtered, because of the paths both siblings took, that relationship slowly deteriorated. Leading them back to square one, such as the game shows.

Sorry if any of this is incorrect. I just thought I’d point out what I believe makes sense, but please feel free to inform me! I have seen nothing of this game apart from Cory’s series and am just going off what his videos have shown! :D

1:30:58 I'm a culture nerd so here's some cultural/historical context for Atsu's lack of affection with her brother:

(‼I understand that she's also carrying resentment for him because of the circumstances, this is just cultural context to explain why she probably wouldn't have been that "affectionate" by Western standards even if she wasn't angry with him.)

The colonization of Ezo began around 1869, at which point physical affection, both public and private, between relatives was not custom in Japan. 

Things like hugging, hand-shaking, kissing, and even saying "I love you", were not adopted into Japanese social customs until the 1940s-1950s from the US occupation. 

Like most east Asian countries, Japanese people express their affections more indirectly through acts of service, writing, gifting, etc. I'm half-Asian, so I can confirm first-hand that this cultural difference is still very much prevalent today.

Hi Cory! I’m currently in the hospital recovering from surgery at the time of writing this, but since I platinumed the game, and since you’re my favorite YouTuber of all time, I figured I’d contribute.
First of all, the most powerful weapon in the game in terms of main weapons is mostly situational. Similarly to Pokemon, some weapons are more effective against certain enemies weapons. Here’s a list:
* Katanas beat Katanas
* Dual Katanas beat Pole arms and Spears
* Yari beats Sickles and Kusarigama
* Kusarigamas beat shields and are good for crowd control 
* Odachis beat Brutes (Aka big dudes)
You will deal bonus damage if you match up the effectiveness based on what you’re fighting. Even so, you can still kill whoever you want with whatever weapon you want. Using the aligning weapons, however, is most efficient. You can also luckily acquire these weapons in whatever order you please, regardless of your direction in the story, so cheers to that.
Second, and equally as important, quick fire weapons. These are essentially throwable weapons or deterrents that deal stagger damage. By far the most powerful and useful of these weapons is the Kunai, and the Tanzutsu (revolver pistol). You can obtain the Kunai in Teshio Ridge from a woman named Hana. She will need help defending her farms, and she will give them to you almost immediately. As for the Tanzutsu, it is only accessible after reaching Oshima Coast. You will get it from a quest called “Guns and Consequences”. Talk to a man named Matchlock Murata, and he will gift you the gun after doing a favor for him. Overall, these deal the highest damage in the shortest amount of time, so it will be incredibly helpful if you need to heal mid-fight. 
Not only that, there are special charms that you can collect thay will give you bonuses for your QuickDraw weapons, such as the “Charm of Burning Blades”, which makes your Kunai deal FIRE damage, “Charm of Hidden Blades” which allows you to throw 3 extra Kunai for one draw, and “Charm of Tanzutsu Guard” which grants you a moderate chance to regain bullets when interrupting an attack with the Tanzutsu.
Now onto Ranged Weapons. The most powerful of these ranged weapons is the Yumi, a large bow and arrow, and the Tanegashima, a matchlock rifle. You can get the Yumi from Ran, or from a quest called “The Legend of Opusnupuri” which gives you both the bow and a charm called “Charm of True Aim”. It allows you to automatically lock onto enemies with the Yumi, guaranteeing headshots every time. AND GET THIS, once you upgrade the charm, the Yumi will lock onto 3 ENEMIES AT ONCE! As for the Tanegashima, it is also only obtained in Oshima Coast. It is unlocked automatically in the story quest “The Storm Breaks”.
Now last but definitely not least, Armor! The most important detail about armor is what kind of player you are. Your specific armor will give you perks, which will be beneficial to your play style. Here’s more details:
- Close Combat Playstyle: Armor of the Undying and Onryo Armor
- Ranged Playstyle: Dragonfly Armor and Ginjis Guard Armor
- Stealth Playstyle: Ninetales Armor, Crimson Kimono, and Fundoshi
- Thrown Weapon Playstyle: Mercenary Attire and Spider Lily Armor
- Parry Playstyle: Bounty Master Armor
- Exploration Playstyle: Robes for Sitturaynu and Taros Armor
But if you’re looking for the best overall Armor in the game, go for The Armor of The Undying. It gives you so many opportunists to counter, attack, heal, and will make you a force to be reckoned with. 
And the best part? Armor of the Undying can be found very early game! Once you unlock free roam in the area Ishikari Plain (Road to Ishikari Plain), talk to the Storyteller Ugetsu, and he will tell you the tale of the Undying Samurai. He will tell you what to do from there. 
And that’s all the helpful info I can give you since I’m short on time at the moment. 
Ive been watching your videos for about 10 years now, so it would mean a lot if this was noticed lol. Thank you so much for reading, and keep being the amazing person you have always been!

Cory, I got you fam

SpringBonnie: easiest to deal with, you’ve handled him well. But when you leave from under a table, don’t use your flashlight, he’ll see it.

SpringFreddy: the one on the stage next to Bonnie. He doesn’t activate unless the power turns off. If that happens, head to the office, and interact with the screen in the back of the office. Then you need to head to the breaker box at the entrance of the building, in the little side room.

FredBear: the sprinter. He’s the one behind the curtain. Keep the curtains closed, or he’ll come for you. If things get really bad, turn the power off and hide. He can see you through the camera system, so no matter where you are, if the power is on, and he comes out, he will know where you are, and he will get you.

Plushtrap: the doll on the desk. If you hide under one table for too long, his programming activates, and, thinking you’re a child being scared, he’ll come to you and sing a song, inadvertently alerting the animatronics to your location. Also, don’t run around the same tables over and over. It’s part of his programming to prevent kids from doing that so they don’t get hurt. (Yes the irony is brazenly clear) So if you go around the same tables again and again, he’ll jumpscare you to get you to stop.

The last night is a real treat, one that I can only minimally prepare you for.

The Thing: if you hear it coming, wait until it is close, then hit it with the flashlight. It’ll melt away. Rinse and repeat.

The ghost kids: do not run into them. They will call the Thing to you, killing you on contact.

The animatronics: they no longer chase you, but stand in hallways to make your progress take longer. Don’t touch them.

Your goal: wait at the computer in the office, the one that controls the power. Wait until the timer winds down until you can head to the breaker I mentioned earlier, then flip the switch. Rinse and repeat until 6 am.

Heya Cory, resident Little Nightmares lore expert here. To give you a basic rundown on what's going on in these games, they take place in a nightmare realm called the Nowhere. Children from our world are lured into this realm by a figure known as the Ferryman with promises of a better life. However, they soon find that the Nowhere isn't at all what he made it out to be. They are hunted, killed, traumatized, and corrupted by the monsters of the realm, known as the Residents. After being thoroughly broken, the children grow up to become Residents themselves. This is what happened to Mono in Little Nightmares 2 after he was betrayed by Six. He grew up alone in the Signal Tower, trapped in a time loop as the Thin Man, forced to endlessly repeat the mistakes of the past that led to Six's betrayal.

Speaking of Six, people who play the Little Nightmares games tend to demonize and portray her as a villain, but the truth is that she endured more trauma in the Nowhere than any of us could possibly imagine, all at only the age of 9. It's heavily implied that she was already mentally disturbed when Mono found her, so it was only a matter of time until she snapped. When she was kidnapped by Thin Man and brought to the Signal Tower, she became trapped in a personalized dreamworld created by the music box. She couldn't see what she had become. While Mono was struggling to save his friend, all Six saw was Mono attacking and dragging her back into the nightmare. In the final bossfight, every time Mono hit the music box, Six would visibly flinch, because he was physically hurting her. When he finally got the last hit in, she crumpled up on the floor crying. That's what pushed her over the edge, and why she ended up dropping him. Although her fate is left ambiguous in the first game, it's easy to assume she grew up to become a Resident.

That's the sad truth of the Little Nightmares games. There is no winning in the Nowhere. You either die young, or grow up (kinda like in real life). That's why the only way to have a happy ending is to escape altogether. All the characters are tragic figures, even the monsters. I’ve been reading through a lot of comments about the ending, and while I totally understand why people are upset, I wanted to share a theory I’ve been piecing together as someone who’s followed this franchise closely.

I think Little Nightmares III is ultimately a metaphor for mental illness and healing, and the ending—while abrupt and bittersweet—lines up perfectly with that idea. Throughout the game, Lo’s journey seems symbolic of someone trying to navigate the darkness of their own mind. The environments, the enemies, the shifting timelines—it all feels like a distorted reflection of internal trauma.

Alone (Wendy), in this theory, isn’t just a friend. She could represent Lo’s emotional support, or even the embodiment of his trauma. The fact that you carry her doll and use it as a mechanic to move between past and present suggests she’s deeply connected to how Lo processes his pain. She’s constantly by his side, helping him progress, and that bond feels essential—not just narratively, but symbolically.

One of the key moments for me is that Lo doesn’t face the final boss alone. He and Alone (Wendy) fight it together. That could represent how emotional support systems—whether people, memories, or even parts of ourselves—can help us confront the darkest parts of our psyche. But after the battle, they’re separated. Alone doesn’t go with him through that final mirror, and Lo is left alone in this quiet, bitter victory.

Here’s where the theory deepens: the mirror, to me, represents reflection and self-realization. The fact that Alone refuses to cross through it might symbolize Lo reaching a point in his healing where he has to move forward without the emotional crutches that once held him together. Not because they weren’t valuable, but because true growth often involves letting go—even of the things that once saved us.

That final scene, where Lo is trying to piece the broken mirror back together, feels like a metaphor for trying to rebuild your sense of self after trauma. Maybe he’s hoping to see his old reflection—one where he wasn’t alone. Or maybe he’s afraid of seeing who he’s become without her. Either way, it’s a powerful image.

So, my theory is that this ending isn’t just dark for the sake of being dark. It’s meant to reflect the real, messy process of healing. Sometimes, even when we overcome what’s holding us back, we don’t come out unscathed. We grow, we survive—but we don’t always get to keep everything (or everyone) that helped us get there.

It’s a heavy message, but an honest one. And to me, that’s what makes this ending so impactful.

that's my analysis of the story so far In Little Nightmares III, the story can be seen as the journey of a boy trapped in isolation who creates an imaginary friend to cope with loneliness and fear. The boy is locked in a small, white room for so long that his mind begins to create a world through imagination and drawings. This world is filled with grotesque adults and twisted environments that represent his perception of reality, exaggerated by fear and trauma. The girl, who appears to be his companion throughout the game, is actually a creation of his mind, born from his need for hope and comfort in a nightmare. She exists to help him survive mentally, to give him courage and companionship, but she is tied to the nightmare itself and cannot exist in the world of peace the boy dreams of. The mirror at the end of the game represents his imagined gateway to peace and freedom. The boy believes that passing through it will finally allow him to escape the nightmare. The girl hesitates and tries to hold him back not out of fear but because she understands that if he escapes into peace, she will no longer exist. During the final scene, when he insists on going through the mirror, she is rejected by it and turns back into the doll, symbolizing the loss of the only connection that kept him sane. She drops a drawing of the two of them being happy together, which the boy did not take with him, symbolizing that in his pursuit of peace, he has forgotten her and left behind the memory of the bond they shared. The ending shows that although he escapes the nightmare and reaches a world of peace, he is still internally sad because he lost the one thing that gave him strength and emotional connection. The post-credits scene of him attempting to rebuild the mirror implies that he still longs to reconnect with her, to restore the lost part of his imagination and regain what he lost, suggesting that the story of his mind and emotions is not yet complete. The boy’s journey is therefore a story of imagination, loneliness, hope, and loss, showing that escaping external nightmares does not always equate to true happiness, and that the emotional cost of survival can be profound and lasting.

Heya Cory, resident Little Nightmares lore expert here. To give you a basic rundown on what's going on in these games, they take place in a nightmare realm called the *Nowhere.* Children from our world are lured into this realm by a figure known as the *Ferryman* with promises of a better life. However, they soon find that the Nowhere isn't at all what he made it out to be. They are hunted, killed, traumatized, and corrupted by the monsters of the realm, known as the Residents. After being thoroughly broken, the children grow up to become Residents themselves. This is what happened to Mono in Little Nightmares 2 after he was betrayed by Six. He grew up alone in the Signal Tower, trapped in a time loop as the Thin Man, forced to endlessly repeat the mistakes of the past that led to Six's betrayal.

Speaking of Six, people who play the Little Nightmares games tend to demonize and portray her as a villain, but the truth is that she endured more trauma in the Nowhere than any of us could possibly imagine, all at only the age of 9. It's heavily implied that she was already mentally disturbed when Mono found her, so it was only a matter of time until she snapped. When she was kidnapped by Thin Man and brought to the Signal Tower, she became trapped in a personalized dreamworld created by the music box. She couldn't see what she had become. While Mono was struggling to save his friend, all Six saw was Mono attacking and dragging her back into the nightmare. In the final bossfight, every time Mono hit the music box, Six would visibly flinch, because he was physically hurting her. When he finally got the last hit in, she crumpled up on the floor crying. That's what pushed her over the edge, and why she ended up dropping him. Although her fate is left ambiguous in the first game, it's easy to assume she grew up to become a Resident.

That's the sad truth of the Little Nightmares games. There is no winning in the Nowhere. You either die young, or grow up (kinda like in real life). That's why the only way to have a happy ending is to escape altogether. All the characters are tragic figures, even the monsters. The true villain of the franchise is whatever eldritch abomination the constant eye symbolism is referring to. So with all that out of the way, we have yet to see what fate is in store for our new protagonists, Low and Alone. Will they be able to escape? Succeed where Mono and Six failed? Or will they also fail? Only time will tell.

Okay the sequence of events from 44:38 to 45:12 is unintentionally cinematic! 
Cory’s got the justified anger to kill the grandmother, so he does, and right as he backs up the killer comes down. Then he takes the shot, but only hears a click. 
Then silent tension: Cory knows he’s dead if the killer turns around. But as the killer leaves, he gets that sense of relief, just for the situation get even worse when he realizes he has *no more bullets.*
In the background, as Cory starts discarding the shells, us viewers hear footsteps going around the room. AND THEN BOOM! Straight jump-scare that ends this series of events beautifully. It’s incredible when a game and a player accidentally act out one of the best horror scenarios I’ve ever seen in an indie game.

Her pursuer having disappeared from sight, Roxanne bangs on a random door, being greeted by the Stranger, who ignores her panicked state and asks her if she would like to come inside. Roxanne then suddenly experiences abdominal pains and again begs the stranger to help her before she begins to spit up blood, a worm-like creature wriggling its way out of her mouth.

Ending C: Mother (IMO the best ending)

Roxanne gains access to the bunker via decoding the puzzle from the clocks, and either finds a vent which ends at a strangely misplaced security room or is knocked out by the Butcher, this time waking up in a cage with mutant hogs feeding on human bodies. Either way, she will find her way further into the facility, all the while avoiding the Butcher and his mutated dog. She discovers that she is inside a research facility hidden below the house, plastered with CFV logos, with private logs revealing that the scientists there had been conducting experiments with radiation there for decades. Roxanne manages to activate the lab's self-destruct system and goes for the exit where she is confronted by the Butcher with a chainsaw. She is able to fend him off as she clears the way out and escapes to safety before the entire area detonates but falls unconscious. She is rescued afterwards and wakes up several days later in a hospital bed, surrounded by a nurse and a doctor, who are apparently unaware of the true nature of what they believe to have been an "accident" and ask her how she is feeling. Roxanne is unable to speak, so the doctor assures her that she'll be back on her feet in around a week and tells her to get some rest for her upcoming surgery tomorrow. That night, while Roxanne is watching TV, she suddenly starts to vomit blood, and a worm-like creature erupts from her mouth. Roxanne faints again and sometime later Roxanne, wakes up to find the whole hospital ward bathed in red and empty safe for a number of pulsating organic egg sacs sprouting on the ground, the beds, the walls, and on top of the ceiling. Roxanne reaches the exit door, at which point the credits roll.

Ending D: Brain

Roxanne gains access to the bunker via decoding the puzzle from the clocks, further progressing deeper into its depths. After discovering an elevator that leads down to the lowest floor, she attempts searching for clues behind the meaning of the CFV corporation. After entering a large work room she follows up the stairs and into a hallway with seemingly random rooms. Some of which are used for brain washing, one is being used for medical procedures, another is a filming studio, and when she goes into the adjacent room, there is a large tesla tower that bursts into function after pulling a large lever. Promptly she follows the cords attached to the structure into the filming studio where she sees a sign warning her not to stare straight into the lens of a mounted video recorder. As her intrusive thoughts take control, she blatantly ignores the warning and proceeds to stare straight into the lens. Roxanne falls into a trance like state and begins wandering in a labyrinth of flesh and brain tissue. In some of the rooms she discovers fleshy egg sacs, while in other rooms she finds colonies of people trapped in some sort of restraint while a large tentacle from the ceiling is covering their whole face and sucking them of nutrients. As Roxanne progresses through the fleshy corridors even further, she finds the room that holds her fate. Three floating creatures appear with large teeth. As she gets close, the camera pans to one of the creatures, the screen goes black and the credits roll.

Feeding the cat will make it so no visitors will appear at your door step during the night, ONLY humans, this is a great time to stock up on people that you KNOW are innocent and that you can offer to the FEMA person who appears at your doorstep. So if you want to make sure the cultists dont get taken since you need ALL three of them alive, save up on FEMA notices and give them to two people to offer. Im pretty sure the cultists are never going to kill anymore, so dont waste your energy on them. 

When the maniac with the gun appears on your door step for the second and third time, he will ask you to prove that youre not a visitor, the first time you should show him your hands and the second time you should show him a picture. BUT!!! the bald guy will appear on your doorstep and tell you about the dirt in your basement, that you can dig out to make a tunnel. The tunnel digging will drain all your energy so make sure to drink a enerJake and wash your hands in the bathroom, since they will be dirty.

SPOILER WARNING ⚠️ 


1.	Yes, I’m Alone (worst)
	•	Let the Super Imposter into the house (either tell him “you’re alone” when he asks, or have no tenants in the house when he shows up). He breaks in and takes you — instant Alone ending.  ￼
	2.	No, I’m not Alone (bad)
	•	Make sure at least one Visitor is in the house when you board up the windows (i.e., don’t purge everyone). When the group turns on you, you’re taken — basement/group ending.  ￼
	3.	Yes, I’m a Murderer (bad)
	•	Reach around day 12 and kill every tenant (even humans). After slaughtering them all you’ll get this ending — paranoia eats the protagonist.  ￼
	4.	Wrath of the Vigilante (bad)
	•	Fail the Vigilante’s test (on his 2nd/3rd visit). Pick any failing test option — Teeth, Armpit, or Photo — you get shot, go mad, and this ending triggers.  ￼
	5.	Shroom or Doom (bad / mushroom route)
	•	Requirements (summary): beat the game once → on night 6 meet the Mushroom Man and take his Book of Smiles page → on day 7 pick the basement mushroom (unlock basement by letting Cat Lady in on night 4) → eat the mushroom → follow the chain (apple on day 8, click bedroom clock day 9, speak to mushroom man at night) → follow him into Mushroom Land on night 10.  ￼
	6.	May Death Cleanse us of Our Sins! (cult ending, ok)
	•	Let the cult leader and his three followers into your house and keep all three alive (avoid FEMA taking any of them; place other guests so cultists keep their seats). When the leader returns, accept his invitation — join the cult.  ￼
	7.	Embrace the Inevitable (ok — dig/tunnel route)
	•	This is multi-step and the most fiddly:
	1.	Watch TV to get the ForRest number; order 2 EnerJeka cans.
	2.	Let Cat Lady in so basement unlocks.
	3.	Reach night 9 and talk to the Prophet.
	4.	Dig in the basement on days 10, 11 and 12; show the Vigilante your eyes (night 10) and hands (night 12).
	5.	Drink an EnerJeka on day 12, use the bathroom mirror prompts, enter the tunnels, turn right to talk to the miner, then jump into the hole he found. This unlocks the burial/tunnel ending.  ￼
	8.	Child of Doom (weird / rare)
	•	A very rare chain: keep a mysterious woman (possibly linked to the protagonist’s past) in your bed, spare her if tested, she appears pregnant at night and dies after childbirth. Then you must find the baby in the house (click several specific environmental spots: right bedroom curtain, ceiling fan in office, bowl under bathtub, then look out the window the same night) — find the baby four times and look out every window that night to trigger this ending.  ￼
	9.	Welcome to FEMA (good)
	•	Be proactive and cooperative with FEMA: use the FEMA hotline when you learn signs, hand out FEMA Notices strategically, and take out at least one Visitor per day (or otherwise make sure FEMA notices you). Cooperate with FEMA officers and you’ll be offered a job — that’s this ending.  ￼
	10.	The End? (best / “survive” ending)

	•	The hardest: reach day 14 with only humans as your tenants. Strategy: use FEMA Notices smartly to remove suspected Visitors, keep reliably human guests alive (recommended: little girl, widowed women who carries her husband around, burnt fireman, tall man), avoid killing humans, and shield your human tenants across FEMA removals (FEMA appears on set nights). If you board up the house on day 14 with only humans inside, you get the best ending.  ￼

As far as I know, there is a randomization of whether or not someone will be Human or a Visitor. There are only a handful of people who will consistently be Human/Visitor regardless of the save file: the tall thin man you first meet will always be Human, the twins, and the fireman. 

The woman with the hunched shoulder that stays in the closet is a Visitor but she doesn’t realize it. She is a passive Visitor so she won’t kill anyone, but if you discover someone has died, you have another Visitor with you. If you let her stay she will actually help you with identifying the other Visitors you have staying with you. However, once you go through all the tests with her, she will come to realization that she is a Visitor and will ask you to kill her. If you don’t, she will just leave without killing anyone. 

As for testing, if someone fails 2 of the tests, you can likely deduce that they’re a Visitor. A Human has the chance of failing one, so try to refrain from jumping to conclusions and immediately killing them.

Hey Cory, let me hit ya up the full fnaf lore, so ya know about it!

The Foundation: Henry Emily (the engineer) and William Afton (the businessman) opened Fredbear’s Family Diner, featuring "springlock" suits that could be worn by humans or operated as robots.
The First Murder: William Afton murdered Henry’s daughter, Charlotte, outside the diner. Her soul possessed the Puppet (Marionette), who became a guardian for future victims.
The Bite of ’83: Afton’s youngest son, often called the Crying Child, died after his head was crushed by the Fredbear animatronic in a prank gone wrong. This event shattered the Afton family and led to the closure of Fredbear's. 
The Missing Children’s Incident (1985)
The Murders: At the new Freddy Fazbear’s Pizza, Afton lured five children into a back room using a yellow Spring Bonnie suit and murdered them.
Possession: The Puppet "gave life" to these children by placing their bodies/souls into the core animatronics: Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, Foxy, and Golden Freddy. 
Sister Location & Remnant (Late 1980s)
Afton Robotics: Afton became obsessed with "Remnant"—a substance created from human souls that could grant immortality. He built "Funtime" animatronics specifically designed to capture children.
Elizabeth’s Death: Afton’s daughter, Elizabeth, was killed by Circus Baby and subsequently possessed the animatronic.
Michael’s Mission: Afton’s eldest son, Michael, was sent by his father to find Elizabeth. He was eventually tricked and "scooped" by Ennard (a fusion of the Funtime animatronics), who used Michael’s body as a disguise to escape. 
The Downfall of William Afton (1990s–2023)
Springtrap’s Birth: Years after the original murders, Afton returned to the abandoned Freddy's to destroy the animatronics. The ghosts of his victims cornered him, forcing him into the old Spring Bonnie suit. The springlocks failed, crushing him to death and trapping his soul inside, where he became Springtrap.
Fazbear’s Fright: In 2023, a horror attraction opened using old props. They found Springtrap, who survived a fire that eventually burned the building down. 
The Final Burning (FNAF 6)
The Lure: Henry Emily returned to end the cycle. He built a fake pizzeria to lure all remaining haunted entities—Springtrap, Scrap Baby (Elizabeth), Molten Freddy (Ennard), and the Puppet.
The Fire: Henry set the building on fire, intending to release all souls and "send Afton to hell". 
The Modern Era (Help Wanted – 2026)
Glitchtrap & The Mimic: Fazbear Entertainment, now a massive corporation, scanned old circuit boards for a VR game, accidentally releasing a digital virus named Glitchtrap. This entity (or a "Mimic" AI copying Afton) possessed a tester named Vanessa.
The Pizzaplex: A massive mall called the Mega Pizzaplex was built over the ruins of the FNAF 6 location.
Current Events (2025-2026): In Security Breach, a boy named Gregory and a modified Glamrock Freddy fought against Vanessa (Vanny) and a reborn Afton-entity (Burntrap). By 2026, the Pizzaplex lies in ruin as seen in the Ruin DLC, where a girl named Cassie searches for Gregory while encountering a dangerous AI system known as the Mimic. 

If ya want it explained differently i got you!

Founding & Early Murders (1970s-80s): William Afton and Henry Emily start Fredbear's Family Diner. Afton begins murdering children, whose souls possess animatronics (Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, etc.) and the Puppet (Henry's daughter, Charlotte).
Family Tragedy: Afton's youngest son, Evan, dies in the Bite of '83 at Fredbear's; his daughter Elizabeth is killed by Circus Baby.
Afton's Demise & Rebirth: Afton is cornered and crushed within the Spring Bonnie suit, becoming Springtrap; later, he survives fires to return as Glitchtrap and Burntrap.
Michael Afton's Journey: William's other son, Michael, works to undo his father's evil, getting scooped by Ennard (fused Funtime animatronics) and later helping Henry burn the remaining haunted animatronics.
Digital Era (FNAF 1-Security Breach): Fazbear Entertainment reboots, leading to new haunted locations and the discovery of Afton's digital consciousness (Glitchtrap) in Help Wanted, possessing a beta tester (Vanny) and infecting the Pizzaplex with the Mimic AI.

This is game is like "Rhythm 0" which was a REAL performance art piece where Marina Abramović stood motionless for six hours in a gallery, presenting herself as a passive object. On a table next to her, there were 72 objects, ranging from harmless items (a rose, a feather, etc) to dangerous ones (scissors, a whip, a knife, a loaded gun with one bullet).

The story revolves around two separate AI programs—M1 and M2—created by Edwin, who were actually the original inventor of the animatronics long before Henry and William came into the picture. M2 was designed as an advanced emotional AI capable of mimicking human personalities and was specifically created to replicate Fiona so their son David would still have a maternal figure while Edwin worked. However, after Fiona and David’s deaths, M2 began taking on David’s personality, which deeply disturbed Edwin. Overcome with grief and guilt from neglecting his son, Edwin grew increasingly unstable and took out his anger on M2, verbally and physically abusing it. As a result, M2 absorbed Edwin’s violent and erratic personality and eventually may have been involved in the explosion that killed Edwin—choosing to leave him to die. Meanwhile, M1 is a separate entity and seems to be either possessed by Fiona’s spirit or somehow programmed with her essence despite never having interacted with her while she was alive. (remember M2 and M1 are different. M2 took on fiona’s personality because it was programmed too, however M1 never was programmed to act like fiona. im not sure what the original purpose of M1 was though.) This is supported by how M1—also referred to as Dispatch—repeatedly contacts Edwin through emails, begging him to complete the schematic meant to stabilize M2’s behavior, seemingly unaware that Edwin is already dead. When Arnold, the current protagonist, refuses to hand over the schematic (in this ending) Dispatch becomes increasingly aggressive, trying to prevent him from going further.  There is also speculation that M1’s code was uploaded into the MXES system by Edwin or someone else, though this remains unconfirmed and there is evidence behind it however i forgot but there’s more information online if y’all would like to know more about that. i also came across a theory that burntrap in security breach isn’t william and instead M2 whilst ‘the blob’ looking thing is M1. this would make sense as to why the blob refused to attack the player and instead chose to attack M2. but that begs the question—what happened to william? is he truly dead this time? there’s so many different outcomes with all of them each having their own solid evidence behind them. The animatronic known as Tiger Rock, found in the basement, is likely possessed by Edwin himself, as the hallucinations associated with it can’t be explained by typical animatronic programming—implying something supernatural. You could make the argument that arnold is just going insane however the things that happen in FNAF ALWAYS Represents something. I don’t think they would dedicate an entire boss fight to arnold just going insane, it’s always something more figurative than just that. Edwin and Fiona were the true originators of the animatronic technology. William and Henry only entered the scene after Edwin’s company went bankrupt, stealing his ideas and reworking them into a cheaper, less stable form. This shortcut led to the infamous springlock failures and ultimately turned William into the half robot half human serial killer he became. In this view, if Edwin’s designs had been honored and properly built upon, none of the tragedies in the series may have happened (aside from edwin’s story 😂). also i noticed that there’s a thematic connection between M1 and the Puppet, both of whom were created to protect their creator’s children but ended up becoming possessed by those they were meant to serve technically. While not the same being, M1 and the Puppet share a hauntingly similar origin. As for M2’s goal, while it may seem like it wants the schematic to upgrade itself or something of the sort i don’t think that this ending is canon because it doesn’t align well with the confirmed events of Security Breach: Ruin, where the Mimic (presumably M2) ends up trapped beneath the Pizzaplex. This raises some inconsistencies, but overall, the theory paints a tragic and layered backstory where Edwin’s grief, corporate betrayal, and unintended consequences spark the dark legacy that unfolds throughout the series. It was never about William or henry, Edwin was the start of it all.

For those who don't know or haven't played this game: 

"Sharks and minnows" is a game a lot of swimming athletes play where one swimmer is chosen to be the shark. The other swimmers have to complete a lap to the otherside of the pool without being tagged/eaten by the shark. If you get tagged, you become another hostile swimmer that has to help the original shark to tag as many swimmers as possible. The last one to survive wins essentially. The game was made to get your adrenaline pumping and motivate swimmers to push their limits and be faster.

This video game takes the original game to the next level by putting you in a "real" situation by making you swim in the dark, and avoid as many other creatures and making you a lone swimmer.

Wow, this might be my favorite game Cory has played this year. I love games like this where a lot of the story/context is left to the audience to decipher, and I feel like there's a lot of amazing details in this game that add to it.

Gonna rant a bit rn: To me, this game is most likely a critique of Japan's work/corporate culture, which is extremely toxic and leaves no breathing room for employees in terms of their outside life, mental health, etc. The barista mentions that she left her toxic corporate job to open the tea shop; as the game goes on and she begins hallucinating, however, a lot of her customers are those who are either ungrateful/downright rude or are corporate workers themselves. Customers (such as Trinity) go from being cordial to ungrateful of her service, mock her for having such an 'easy' job, unnecessarily criticize her work ethic, etc. 

My theory is that considering her hallucinations, throughout the game the barista is also hallucinating her interactions with her customers. I'm not implying that they're not there and she's talking to herself, but rather hallucinating what they're saying and connecting it to her past in the corporate world, which likely left her with some mental health issues. One of the strongest pieces of evidence for this, in my eyes, is the CEO customer; he not only mentions being in the corporate world himself, but also a female worker who "ran away" from her responsibilities. I think the worker this customer mentions may be the barista: Considering Japan's extremely toxic work culture, the fact that she quit her job to run her own business may have been seen as "running away" from the responsibilities she's expecting of completing as, frankly, a slave to the corporation she worked at. 

I believe the barista may have developed her mental health issues from her experience as a corporate worker, and as a result, is reflecting much of what she experienced before in what's supposed to be her 'dream' job. She mentioned at the end that she thinks everyone is constantly judging her and views her as a failure, which may unfortunately be true due to (from my understanding) Japanese work culture placing a high emphasis on how dedicated one is to their job. I'd imagine leaving that type of world would be labeled as a failure, sadly.

I may be looking too much into this, but I found this game really interesting and I like to over-analyze things. Thanks for playing Cory!

My takeaway on this game after watching you (yes YOU, Cory) play this amazing game:

You board the bullet train. You pass out while on the train from a deep vain blood clot (diagnosed by the doctor in Ending 2.) You play as your spirit trying to get back into your human body: the gameplay of looping on the train is you trying to find a way to get back into your body and wake up. The train crashes into a boy and his sister while you’re still unconscious, killing them both. You meet both the boy’s and the sister’s spirits while you’re stuck looping. I think that they noticed another spirit (you) on the train and disguised themselves as passengers to try to help you stay alive, explaining why they are sitting at row 4, as they are dead, and also explaining why you can only interact and talk with those two, as they are also spirits, with exception for the old man later in the gameplay, also explaining why the old man states that you are not “human” because you are a spirit. This might also suggest that the old man is also a spirit, and might be dead, since you can interact with him, and since he stated that no one responded to him on the train except you.

At the end of the game, you figure out the solution to end the looping after talking with the sister. Both of you conclude that running different directions on the train at the same time will end the looping, but before you do, you get to either choose to run toward the green car or toward the regular car. I think the green car is the afterlife and the regular car is your human body. If you choose to run toward the green car, you end the loop by going to heaven, but this also means you die with the boy and his sister (Ending 1). However, if you choose to run toward the regular car, you escape death as you get chased by the grim reaper. You then meet with the boy’s and his sister’s spirit to say one final goodbye. I think the boy gets a little attached to you after what you guys have been through, so he asks if you want to come with them, in other words, if you want to die with them, however, the sister disagrees and says “It’s not your time yet” since you just escaped death. Finally, you enter the regular car (your body) and wake up from being unconscious, overhearing that a woman and her brother (the two spirits you met while unconscious) were involved in “the accident” (the train hitting them). I also think the last scene of the boy and his sister was either to show them going to heaven or to confirm that they were the ones that got hit from the bullet train since they were walking on train tracks (Ending 2).

Hopefully this made sense. Let me know if I missed anything.

I think one of the biggest problems with some horror games nowadays is that developers think that complicating the lore / how you get the lore is the same as giving the story depth. In my opinion, Amanda is one of the biggest perpetrators of this. Behind all the complicated puzzles is a story that isn’t even worth doing the puzzles for. Don’t get me wrong, the story is fine but it’s not worth (imo) spending hours upon hours searching and solving puzzles for. Imagine how much better the game could be if instead of focusing on finding the most obscure ways to hide lore, the devs focused on telling a more straightforward narrative that was easier for players to digest. Scrambling around the pieces of a story doesn’t make the story better - it just makes it more annoying to solve.

Fun facts about Yasuke cuz I did a bunch of research as a black and Japanese person studying this in college: Yasuke was an actual person! He was a sort of body guard for Father Valignano, a Portuguese Jesuit who was trying to spread Christianity to Japan. Nobunaga was considered to be the most powerful warlord, hence why the Jesuits went to “ask” Nobunaga to move around more freely. Oda Nobunaga legit thought Yasuke was such a cool looking person, and the fact that he was able to learn Japanese relatively quickly, Nobunaga was like “aight, I need this dude to train and learn more Japanese,” so Yasuke was a sort of gift to Nobunaga from the Jesuits, mostly to be on his good side. Nobunaga was already uneasy with the Jesuits for many reasons, but I won’t go into it here.

Yasuke went on to go to many battles as a samurai for Nobunaga, mostly against shinobi of different feudal lords (ninjas like that were new at the time, similar to what we think of guerrilla warfare. They thought of it like witchcraft!) It’s believed Yasuke was even gifted a house and land by Nobunaga, only given to the people the strongest warlords trusted and respected. 

Also, when people first saw Yasuke, they either thought he was a demon or a sort of time god, cuz that time god was said to have black skin like his. (Dragon ball fans, that’s partly why Mr Popo has such dark skin. Hyperbolic time chamber and all that)

If you want to read a book about it, I highly recommend “African Samurai” by Thomas Lockler and Geoffrey Girard! The book does a great job explaining modern history and Yasuke/Japanese history! Edit; spelled Lockler wrong

Another edit: I am aware of Lockley and the book being “historical fiction”. I wanted to let you know that the book says many many times that the reader should “take things with a grain of salt,” and that not everything is straight up fact in it, even if it does take some historical letters and such. I actually think it does a good job of essentially saying “hey, we don’t know all the facts, but here’s what we personally theorize.” The book is meant to make you think, that’s all. It’s not trying to sell you something as factual. I was aware of that when I read it, and I don’t personally think Lockley was trying to “lie” to people, although I recommend anyone to read/do their own research with the book if you’re interested. All that I wanted to highlight was that Yasuke did exist, even if historians differ on the context of his story and him as a person/the role he played in Nobunaga’s life

I just searched what Amenti means, so according to google, In Egyptian mythology, it means "The Underworld" or "Realm of the dead". it also says the that its a place where the souls go through trials and tribulations, determining their fate. So in theory, Amenti its not hell yet because the souls are still in purgatory.

This part here 6:12, is a scene from the "Book of the Dead", specifically "Weighing of the heart" Ceremony from the Papyrus of Ani. In conclusion, its a ceremony where Anubis who oversees the person's heart whose conscience and Moral actions and Ma'at, The Goddess of Truth and Justice. If the heart is less heavier than the feather, they are deemed worthy of entering the afterlife. 

Another fact, Duat which also means realm of the dead. The difference between the two is that Amenti is a specific location while Duat is the name of the underworld, and the one who is currently being ruled by Osiris The god of the afterlife or the Deceased.

There is also another theory for Amenti which was said to be a "Hall of Mirrors" which is an illusion and can only be passed through with enough knowledge and wisdom.

Here’s a quick recap of the story so far:
Playtime Co. is a company created by Elliot Ludwig. This company was known for taking in orphans and giving them a home where they had access to all things necessary for their development. The public didn’t know that in actuality Elliot and Playtime Co. were experimenting on the orphans and turning them into toys (that’s why there are no bodies, but a lot of bloody toy parts all across Playtime Co.). The point of this was for whoever is The Prototype to try and live forever. The Prototype is still unknown. And he is collecting all of the dead toys and adding them to himself to become a “god”. The toys worship him because they see him as such. Specifically, when Catnap was a child he was severely sick/injured, The Prototype saved him from his sickness by turning him into a toy, so Catnap was always loyal to The Prototype. We play as an old employee returning to right our wrongs (that’s why most of the characters already know us). There was an event called the “Hour of Joy” where all of the toys retaliated and slaughtered almost all of the employees. Cory, I will give you tips to help you.

1. When you go to open the trunk, message your dad and INSTANTLY go outside to open the trunk, but when you close the trunk, it will make noise so you might wanna hide at the side of the house.
2. Next you want to grab the hose my walking up to the end of it(by the Christmas Tree,) and put it in the barrel and turn the hose on, but to do this without the dad seeing you, you need message him, and you also have to message him again when putting it back. I'd recommend doing this RIGHT after the mom waters the tree so you have plenty of time.
3.  The clean rag is used to wipe the control panel but you need to find the anti-fat spray which is usually located in the kitchen.
4. In the kitchen you need to grab the meat which ALWAYS spawns in 1 of the bottom drawers in the refrigerator. You should ring the doorbell and put it in the microwave and run back to your room. (it don't matter if you leave it in, she won't notice.)
5. In the kitchen you need to turn the fan off and remember the code, then turn it back on. To find the code you look at the first number with starts with the arrow, then go from there and then you'd have a 3 digit code. This is to log into the dads computer.
6. In the room behind the dad, if you open the cabinets, you'd see a hiding spot and a safe. Go into the safe and see which color is in the middle, then you go into your rubiks cube and put in the exact pattern to whichever color is in the middle on the safe.
7. When she waters the Christmas tree, you should wash the rag and PUT back the powder in the same spot after you used it, hide. Make sure to take the rag out and leave the washing machine door open.
8. You can get 3 or 4 batteries out of the flashlight, I think its 3 and you can put it in the radio and turn it on. Your mom will go in there and you can move the shelf and lock her in. But for this to work, you need to find the sleeping pills and put them in the dads drink or else he'll let her out. ONLY do this when you're about to open the gate using the control panel. Then leave and escape.
9. When you find the screwdriver, you can go to the broom in the bathroom and unscrew the bottom of it to get a extra step in the ladder outside. You then need to nail the steps together then hammer them in after you find the hammer.
10. You can honestly just ring the doorbell over and over and your mom will get mad and leave the house to see who's ringing it, then you can just escape that way. That's the easiest ending.

Roof: The ladder that you saw. Find that last step along w/ the missing one you had. A toolbox/repair kit in the house can help, I think. You need those nails to keep those steps intact as you climb. You will end up in the attic. You will see a nail puller, grab it and use it to get on the roof. Once you're on top, you'll walk and see a haystack on the other side of the fence. Jump into it and ya freeee.

Front Door: Ring the doorbell sooo many times (18 diff times (yes, I know, it's a lot, I'm sorry 😭)) to where the mom will become so frustrated, go outside, leave the front gate open, and keep walking. Before she turns around to go back into the house, go behind her and MAKE A RUN FOR ITTTT.

Backyard Ending: Pretend you're doing the Rooftop Ending. You gather all the items and go up there, but instead of heading for the haystack, you look for electric wires most likely on your right near the side of the house. Since you will be walking on them, make sure to grab a balancing tool that helps you stay balanced. That dog will also see you, so before you climb the ladder and all, get meat from the fridge, heat it up in the microwave, and give it to the dog to keep him distracted.

I think there is an alarm that goes off when 1 hops the fence..? If there is, you must ensure that you disable it first. The control panel is hidden near the front door, by the kitchen.

I noticed something really interesting that I haven’t seen anyone bring up, and i might be looking too much into this but with how symbolic this game is I think it’s something that was set up intentionally. If I’m not mistaken, there’s a part in the dialogue that Swansea says something along the lines of “A good captain goes down with his ship/crew.” And as normal and stereotypical as it sounds, it actually made me notice something in the final scene. Right before the credits, we obviously see that Jimmy took Curly to the cryopod and froze him right before he took the cowards route and took his own life instead of just taking responsibility. And yeah it’s a really dark ending, but it fits with what Swansea said about the good captain. Jimmy as obviously a piece of shit and a horrible captain, but he went down with his ship and crew. He died alongside everyone else, and in terms of Swansea’s statement, that would make him a good captain. It resembles how he so desperately wanted to be a good captain and take control, and it resembles how badly he clung to his ego even until the very end, and in his eyes, he fixed everything by basically killing everyone and taking control of all of their deaths instead of just taking responsibility for all the shit he did. Let’s be honest, if Jimmy had been an actual “good captain” he would’ve just taken responsibility for his actions and faced the music, and that way the game would’ve ended on a somewhat good note. But back to the whole “good captain goes down with his crew” thing, we obviously all know Curly was a much better captain, infact he was a REALLY good captain, but instead of going down with his ship/crew, he got put in the cryopod and “survived”. Curly didn’t go down with his ship, and it resembles how despite being a great captain, he still made a horrible decision that ended in a domino effect until everything spiraled and left off with everyone BUT curly, dead. If curly had just taken responsibility one last time, and confronted jimmy about what he had done instead of trying to fix it, NONE of this would’ve happened. Now I’m not saying it was all his fault, but in a way his actions had consequences, and the consequence is that if he DOES get saved, he has to live with the guilt that because he said “I can fix it,” he ultimately just caused an event that killed his entire crew and left his ship destroyed. Jimmy and curly were both bad captains in their own way, and the thing that connects them is that they both had the “I can fix it” mentality that ultimately just made everything worse. Curly said he could fix the problem with Jimmy, and it led to jimmy crashing the ship and putting on a mask that said “good captain”. And when he put that mask on, he kept saying “I’ll fix it, I’ll take care of it.” and his final words were, “ I fixed this.” despite ultimately just ruining everything. Curly was the BETTER captain, but they were both bad captains. The difference is that Jimmy put on a mask and refused to believe it, while curly has to live with the guilt that HE did this.

To those confused, the plot, as written in Wikipedia:

During a routine shipment, the Pony Express freighter spaceship Tulpar is sabotaged into crashing into an asteroid. The crew – consisting of captain Curly, co-pilot Jimmy, medic Anya, mechanic Swansea, and last-minute intern Daisuke – survive. However, most of the ship's resources are blocked off by airbag-like foam, damage to which could potentially breach the ship's hull and trigger lethal decompression. Curly is also mutilated by the crash and cannot speak or move; he is kept alive via a dwindling supply of painkillers. Jimmy declares himself acting captain as a result, claiming that Curly caused the crash after going postal.
When food and medical supplies begin to run low after two months, the crew decides to open their confidential shipment in the hope that it has supplies they can use. But discover that it consists solely of mouthwash which will poison them if they continually consume it. Swansea decides to break his sobriety and consumes the mouthwash due to its alchohol content, the increasing intoxication of Swansea inflaming tensions further. Jimmy, who has been forced to feed Curly the painkillers because Anya continually can't bring herself to do so, attacks and force feeds him in a rage.
Eventually, Anya locks herself in the medical bay with Curly. After failing to convince a drunken Swansea to help him break in, Jimmy knocks him out with the ship's sole bottle of rubbing alcohol and sneaks into the utility bay to find tools. After discovering that Swansea was guarding the ship's only working cryopod, Jimmy believes that Swansea was saving it for himself, and coerces Daisuke into crawling through a damaged vent to reach Anya and Curly. Daisuke makes it through, but is severely injured in the process. Due to the missing rubbing alchohol, Jimmy uses the mouthwash as an impromptu antiseptic, only for it to worsen Daisuke's pain and injuries. Swansea, who despite early annoyed behaviour towards him, had come to care for Daisuke, choosing to reluctantly and crudely euthanize him with a fire axe. Jimmy goes into the medical bay, where Anya is revealed to have killed herself via an overdose. Jimmy finds the ship's emergency revolver and is then attacked by a vengeful Swansea.
Flashbacks to the days leading up to the crash reveal that the Tulpar crew were due to be laid off following their delivery due to Pony Express going out of business. At his birthday party, Curly breaks the news prematurely, distressing his crewmates as he would be given a recomendation for a high paying job afterwards, Jimmy believing Curly to be abandoning the crew to pursue a better career. Later, in a private conversation with Curly, Anya reveals that she is pregnant with Jimmy's child, it being implied that Jimmy raped her. Curly attempts to ease tensions with Jimmy, only for Anya to reveal her pregnancy to Jimmy behind Curly's back. Curly confronts Jimmy but tries to excuse his actions due to their history together. Jimmy convinces Curly that him being punished will make things worse for the crew, Curly choosing to let him go. The stress of his impending layoff, his jealousy of Curly, and the possibility of being held accountable for Anya's pregnancy after the delivery, are ultimately what drives Jimmy to crash the "Tulpar" in a failed murder-suicide bid, Curly's injuries being a result of him trying to save the crew by stopping it from crashing.
Jimmy is hunted down by Swansea, hallucinating that the ship has become a maze, and later finding himself in a graveyard where he has to fight off Swansea. Jimmy uses the revolver to kill Swansea, who in his final moments, condemns Jimmy's cowardice and selfishness while admitting to his own faults, with it being implied that the cryo pod was actually intended for Daisuke. His sanity rapidly declining, Jimmy holds a mock birthday party with the crew's corpses. He proceeds to cut off and consume part of Curly's leg, then force-feeds the captain his own flesh in a surreal hallucination. After a series of additional visions where he is chased by a deformed mass of horse statues, Jimmy finds himself confronted by the Pony Express mascot 'Polle', who mocks him for his faults and actions. Jimmy concludes that he can redeem himself if he ensures Curly's survival, placing him in the cryopod. He then apologizes to Curly for hurting him before killing himself with the revolver, believing he has successfully fixed their situation. The game's credits roll as Curly is placed into a 20-year cryosleep, his fate left uncertain.

Here is everything you might've easily missed that you should know about the game.

1. The doll being in a gift box looking like the casket in which Ron is in.
2. The dad being haunted in the hotel references the attempt to free him from the dolls master.
3. The door slamming 14 times in the intro referencing the 14 days after Rons passing.
4. The doll's and the mom's twisted neck referring to his death.
5. The "grown up conversation" that Ron eavesdrop in the beginning of the game is the one in the end in which the mom leaves him.
6. The thing that mister red face puts in the closet in the beginning is Rons body.
7. The end shows the way in which the body of the other children were stored with the first one being by fire, second one being buried and the third one was put in the back of a car.
8. The spell being the motel card which Ron tossed into the room where his mom was being questioned by the police, meaning when the doll said it was the way to defeat Mr. Red Face he wasn't lying.
9. The doll mentions that its neck deformity is nothing compared to the flaw of the other dolls, implying the other children we see died in a worse way than Ron.
10. The woman in the closet references the 2002 logo.
11. The light stops flickering the moment Ron dies which is supposed to represent his heartbeat.
12. The doll's Master represents how the abusive dad acts like an abusive Master towards Ron, so the doll"s master is in fact Mr. Red Face. That's also why you see the scene of Ron's death transitioning into Mr. Red Face holding the doll.
13. The mother sees Ron during nighttime as a ghost for example when she found him in the closet, not knowing he's a ghost. It's like this in the Vietnamese culture ( the creators of the game are Vietnamese ), during nighttime souls can be seen, but during daylight they can't, that's why the mother finds the kid's dead body during daytime, because she couldn't find him cause his ghost couldn't be seen.
14. The dad is Mr. Red Face because your face turns red when you drink too much, that's also why the mother made up that name, because she sees his dad like that all the time, with a red face.
15. The story is based on a true story which took place in 2017.
16. At the start when Ron received the doll, they couldn’t open Ron’s closet because his stories deny it.
17. Ron entered the afterlife trough his parent's closet, and the cat was an angel.
18. His mother said that if he was good, Mr. Red Face would give him a gift, she meant that she always believed that the father would at least do something good for his son, because the boy was still too young and she didn't want the boy to have a bad opinion of his father.
19. I'm not sure about this one but I think the magic trick about the spaghetti which kept reappearing is because he was a ghost and wasn't actually eating the food, but the doll made him think he ate it.
20. Every single encounter with mister red face is a hint:
-The doll slamming the bottle on the table and turning into red face being a nod to the dad turning into red face.
-The first encounter at night is the dad killing Ron.
-The floating doll shows you Ron's perspective of his murder.

For Cory and those confused: Hamelin was a town that hired a man (later to be referred to as the Pied Piper of Hamelin) to use his flute in order to get rid of the rats that infested and overrun their town. When he did what he was asked to do, the townsfolk cheated him out of the reward, so as a means of exacting revenge, the Pied Piper came back later that same year and led the children of the town away from their houses with his flute, and depending on the version you read, he either led them through a portal, drowned them in the river of Weser, or led them into a cave to kill them. This explains why the Hameln logo is a rat, why there's a rat running around in game, and why the children are hypnotized upon starting up the show (there most likely is a hypnotizing aspect to the Hameln opening music). The fact that their slogan is "follow us to fun" just further proves the theory. What Hameln does with the kids is debatable, though I believe they are using the kids for something demonic, because Rebecca says the names of demons Bael, Paimon, and Balam three times to summon them.

After passing the Calvary near the [sic] Koppenberg they disappeared forever". Although this is obvious, this probably means Hameln was dishonest about their business with Sam and Rebecca Colton, and cheated them out of the reward they promised when making Amanda the Adventurer into a cartoon show. There is a more direct and depressing way you can interpret the scene where Amanda, or Rebecca as she seems to actually be, asks you to help the lonely kitten. It's possible that the demonic entity controlling Amanda/Rebecca and the show is at this point paying very little attention to her since it knows her chances of escaping are slim to none. Sort of like how you'd feel comfortable turning your back on a dog that's locked in a cage. When Amanda/Rebecca asks you, "Will you help the lonely kitten?", she most likely is really trying to say, "Will you help me?", gesturing to the kitten and using it in place of herself in an attempt to deceive the demon because she's secretly begging you to help her. To free her from its control and let her soul finally rest.

Why else would she become increasingly frantic and worried as you continue to deny her request? What other reason could there be for the glitches becoming redder and more intense, as if the demon is beginning to pay increasingly close attention to what she is saying?

When she has that mental breakdown after the third denial and everything becomes glitched out and red, that's the demon realizing what she was actually asking and then punishing her for it by raising her in the air before contorting her "body". Then when the screen cuts to black and then to Amanda/Rebecca's eyes being replaced by many other eyes, that is the demon seizing more control over her and then repeating her request as if to mock her and you before coming for you next.

Hey Cory! Love the videos as always. I believe there are five or six total secret tapes that you can collect to help get additional endings and lore. The secret tapes are colorful vs the standard dark grey vhs episodes. Some tips:

- Give the doll her favorite color flower
- Remember the musical notes on the 24/7 store poster above the cards
- When playing the Family (farm) episode that involves the weather wheel toy, pause the episode during each extreme weather warning and interact with the toy. Don’t worry about the times and locations. Your end goal is to land on each weather wheel option once, and in the correct order, to eventually open it. You may need to guess something wrong here or there during the episode to land on the 3rd weather option on the wheel. It’s harder to see what is vs the thunderstorm and tornado because *hint* it’s covered in cobwebs.
- In that same episode, when you’re prompted to answer what a daddy chicken is called, type in “Sam” instead of “rooster”. There’s a reason why Amanda sounds a bit different when she notices the daddy chicken.

* Also, this isn’t a hint, but a smaller piece of lore. Regardless of the ending you get, take a closer look during the rolling credits. Someone’s name is continuously blocked out. I wonder whose it is…

Hope this helps without spoiling too much of the gameplay. Can’t wait for Part 3!

Fun fact, Kisaragi Station is not a station in Japan but actually an urban legend tale of a girl who fell asleep on the train, missed her stop and traveled dimensions. The girl ended up at a place called "Kisaragi Station" which does not truly exist and where she had said her location was near was next to Japan's "dead bodies mountain." It is believed that therefore, this Kisaragi Station was the land of the dead. The girl was never seen again after her phone lost charge, however it was mentioned that she said she had met an old man there before she disappeared. I think this game was a pretty cool twist to that telling, the wife resembling the girl and the teacher resembling the old man.

I think this game is about a grieving man struggling to accept the passing of his wife. The line, "you're here too early" makes me think that she's telling him he's not ready for the afterlife after attempting to take his own life because the grief was too much to bear. The characters you meet as you play the game could possibly be people that have died too, and you are taking the train with them to the afterlife; but this isn't your stop, not yet at least.

I think the game is about the acceptance of loss. The man’s repetition of going to the station, using the bathroom, buying the applejuice and smoking before getting on the train could represent how often we take for granted the comfort of repetition and stability in our lives until it’s gone, and I think Eiko was represented by the woman who always rode the train with him, and how he didn’t bother to reach out until it was too late. He presence was comforting but because she was part of the routine, he never notice how much he needed her company until it was gone. (That’s shown by him finally talking to her, and her insisting that it was too late even just to talk about her problems.)

The first missing stop represented how loss can easily upset a schedule even if you try to prevent it, and it being the conductor’s fault frames it in a way that represents the guilt and remorse always being easier to blame than yourself. The cicada man represents how grief can stand in the way of doing things that need to be done, so much so that it feels like a physical barrier holding you back. 
The little girl napping with the main character represents the search for familiarity in a foreign place, and her forgetting what her dad looks like represents how grief can swallow you until the person you’ve lost isn’t even the priority anymore, it’s the crippling loneliness of being afraid and suddenly left behind.
Meeting the old man represents finding someone who motivated you and realizing that who they are now, after succumbing the grief, is so vastly different from who they really are, and how it takes finding someone like that to truly acknowledge that you’re not too far gone.
I think the woman standing on the tracks was a hallucination, and that suicide was how Eiko died.
I think the main character tried to kill himself in the end too, but was saved by the idea that ending his own life from grief wasn’t what his wife would have wanted, eventually leading him to change his ways and turn his life around
To be honest, if chilla's art and puppet combo made a game together the story would be AMAZING.

The person posting and people responding interacted, giving her advice on what to do and such. Anyways, the train arrived at “Kisaragi Station” (a place that does not exist) and her situation became more ominous and such, until a man offered to give her ride and she accepted. So, for anyone who doesn’t know, “Ubume” are yokai of women who died during childbirth. (Yokai are a type of spirits, in Japanese folklore, who differ in behavior as well as their appearances.) It’s common to bury the fetus with the mother, who has died during childbirth, and place it in the women’s arms as if she’s hugging her child. Though, in some regions of Japan, it is not legal to cut out the fetus. So, as an alternative, a doll is placed in the arms of the mother, instead of the child. This could’ve been why there were dolls in the apartment rooms. Though, it’s still kinda unclear why the monk wanted to create an Ubume.

Hey Cory, in most areas you can find optional rooms, most of these will have signs on them saying "Storage" or "Utility" Some might even be locked, so you have to find another way round. These contain resources and items to sell in the shop, some even include weapons. One weapon you missed was the Skunk Gun (Pistol Shotgun) back in the basement when you first met the long neck egg enemies. when you get the fuse you needed to take it back to the start to use it on another door. Luckily, the Skunk Gun appears in multiple optional rooms, so you should eventually get it. The Skunk Gun is easily one of the most powerful guns in the game.

What's interesting is Elias says "I know everything about this place" and also "I know someone who can help us", then proceeds to take Jacob to the girl who killed his partner even though she JUST arrived that same day as Jacob. How does Elias know of her capabilities if she just got there?

Cory, a tip is to use the GRP to throw enemies back or into eachother to stun the thrown and hit, and buy you some distance.
OR, if you wanna play aggressively, then you can use the GRP to bring them close, because dropping them still stuns, which opens them up for an attack even at close range. Just don’t drop them on even level.

The security drones are killable, just make sure you shoot their HEAD and nothing else. Even with your pistol, you can kill them and avoid the whole “stealth game” side of the Terminators.

This game’s combat is very much “Think fast, stay alive”.

Another tip, Our favorite space horror game Dead Space’s weakness still applies here. Cut off their limbs, or in this case, shoot off their legs. Put a few in one and it’ll severely hinder the advance.

You have to remember, the entire driving force behind Atreus's current decision making is the fear of losing his father. Ever since he saw that prophecy, it's been all he can think about. Keep in mind as well, this is coming on the heels of his mother's death (you don't magically get over the absence of your mother in 3 years, especially when you're still a child), so he's likely terrified of being left alone in the world with no direction. Plus, Angrboda told Atreus he couldn't say anything about Iron Wood or what he saw etc., so it's not like Atreus can just come out and tell his father. And he's frustrated, because he feels like he's being made to be responsible in ways his father hasn't always been. He resents his hypocrisy to a degree, which is why he's unable to resolve the difference between the secrets he's keeping and the ones his parents kept.

All in all, he's acting like a normal teen. He wants to be respected and heard, after a childhood of being forced to respect and listen to everyone around him (in the way that parenting is essentially "forcing" a child to conform to a standard). And Kratos is not a good father lol, no matter how you wanna slice it. He wants to be, the desire is definitely there, but the man was never even a child himself and his first one died before he could actually raise her. He has no idea what he's doing. The man kept his son's identity from him for 11 years out of fear and shame, he kept the history and lineage of his mother a secret, he even lied by omitting his own lineage and past history because he thought his son would follow in his footsteps. I mean good grief, it took Kratos 11 years to start calling his son by his own name instead of just "boy". 

In contrast, Atreus is really going through it for such a young kid. Half of his suffering was due to the secrets his parents both kept, he's having to endure his father's principled discipline without a mother to balance it with nurturing love and affection, he has no idea who he is or why the giants prophesied that he was such an integral part of the way the timeline is supposed to unfold (which is a pretty big deal), he grew up in complete isolation with no friends or any opportunities to become properly socialized, and just about every person or living creature is trying to kill him or his father in front of him. He's 14. He's literally a child, having endured probably one of the most dysfunctional upbringings a child possibly could. Go back and look at the story trailer for the first game, and look at the number of deep scars Atreus has all over his face at _11 years old._ Watch the opening scene, as he tries to escape his circumstance with two wooden figurines, playing in the snow.

He didn't ask for any of this.

Edit: Some of you grew up in very dysfunctional households with extremely toxic and unrealistic standards and it shows in your lack of empathy for a literal 14 year old child lol, who's father is probably the most impregnably stoic man in all the 9 realms lol (to a clear and absolute fault).

Hey there Cory, if you plan on continuing this, allow me to give you a few tips:

Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, and Foxy only roam round the pizzeria, these are random, but the mechanic is that they go in groups. As you may have learned, you have to find subtle changes in the atmosphere or movement, in order to find out who it is.

The marionette is a bit different, you can never see the marionette as it hides in the roof so you can only hear the melody that it plays. It also roams around, so you must find flickering lights or left hand prints whenever it moves, basically the same as the four.

Ballon Baby is the easiest in my opinion, in order to find out if he is haunted or not, you must check the stability. If his numbers start to glitch out, that’s how you know it is him.

The Way I Play: I have already beaten the whole game, so allow me to give you some tips. To start off I always bring the marionette into the conveyor belt and don’t touch it. (Doing so gets rid of the hardest character to keep track of so I only have to focus on BB and the four.) after doing that you continue your investigation is normal, as long as you are quick enough with finding the animatronics the stability will not go down faster than you finish the night. (Later on in the nights, the animatronics move around faster so I recommend staying in the main dining area, wait until you can pinpoint at least two or less and then follow them around the pizzeria.)

Things to note: Marionette and balloon baby never show up on cameras. Keep an animatronic in the conveyor belt to prevent possession. The only way an animatronic can kill you is if the stability is 0 or if you call a possessed animatronic into the conveyor belt. If a haunted animatronic is in the “Break_Room”, you will hear the phone ring.

Dear Cory,

     I am Reiley Martin. I have watched you ever since I was a child. Through all of my parents and relatives saying "That guy just yells at everything, he's too loud." I still watched. You have been my idol and mentor. You were there for me when my parents split, when my dad moved away from me and my family, when I went to the hospital, when I graduated Middle School, during the pandemic, all of it. I want to thank you for that. You kept my spirits up. But I need you. One last time, before I graduate. We all need you. You keep leaving us with no note, no check up, no letting us know you're ok.
