Just a Tweet every once and a while. My Grandpa just had to go into surgery for cancer to be removed and he is now back in the Hospital because he has internal bleeding. My Grandma is going into surgery for her back. If I can share this with 13.5M people, then you can at least give us something. We will all wait here for you because that's what we do, we know how to wait for you, and we will wait for you for the rest of our lives, because you're worth waiting for. Love you man.

Yours sincerely,

Reiley Martin

For anyone wondering what the peom really means: The poem begins with contrasting imagery: "Little brother burns hot, and the older sister exhales a blue breath." This might symbolize the intense emotions or situations surrounding Tonako, with 'burning hot' suggesting anger or passion, and 'blue breath' hinting at sadness or coldness. These familial figures highlight Tonako's feeling of helplessness, as she "can't do anything" and is "leaving alone."


The line "Not a ray of light can be seen in the darkness" sets a tone of despair and hopelessness. The speaker questions whether they see a "monster" and notes that "Even if I invite him, he doesn't move," suggesting a feeling of being trapped or unacknowledged in their struggle.


The poem continues with "The ugly side casts off the vestiges," indicating a shedding of pretense or facade, revealing a raw and possibly unpleasant reality. The mention of "no island or color ahead" adds to the sense of bleakness and aimlessness.


The line "One bone of a wanderer who couldn't keep up with the white rabbit" seems to reference a lost or failed journey, perhaps alluding to a missed opportunity or the inability to reach a fantastical or better place. The questioning of "Who is changing? Is it me? Or is it someone else?" reveals a deep introspection and confusion about identity and transformation.


The final lines, "Even if you put the monster beside you, reflection of the mirror only shows darkness," and "I fall, and I fall, and yet I haven't fallen," evoke a sense of endless descent without resolution, reinforcing the theme of perpetual despair. The poem ends with "There's nothing at my destination," emphasizing the futility and emptiness that Tonako feels.


Poetry is subjective and open to multiple interpretations, so others may see different meanings in this poem.

Have you noticed how The Stalker seems to drink so much milk? It's actually a common phenomenon linked to villainous characters in popular media. Adults drinking milk can symbolize the defeat of innocence and represent the corruption of human values and social norms. Classic films have shown heroes consuming milk as a sign of purity, while modern depictions of antiheroes and villains often involve them drinking milk. The choice to have characters drink milk could allude to a lack of maturity or arrested development, portraying the frustration of individuals stuck in a less carefree and nurturing world. It can symbolize a desire to return to simpler times, like childhood, when life was less complex and more cared for. And as I said, It could represent a longing for peace and comfort in a world that is often harsh and unforgiving. Such characters might see milk as a source of nostalgia and innocence, a symbol of an unattainable utopia. Whether it's Anton Chigurh, Javier Bardem's character in No Country For Old Men, or Daniel Plainview in There Will be Blood, these characters' milk consumption could represent the defeat of purity and innocence by evil. Chilla's Art might have included the use of milk in The Stalker for a reason, as it is often used as a symbol of a character's twisted nature and the loss of humanity.

Cory, here are some tips:Always remember to use your environment to your advantage like pushing people into walls, throwing bottles, or kicking items off the floor if you have environmental mastery. When you’re going against a group of enemies, try constantly switching targets when attacking to keep your distance from the majority of them. When fighting empowered enemies, (If you fail to complete a finisher on someone), it’s best to wait for their unblockable attacks,(When their arm or leg glows orange), and dodge their attack to stun them for a bit so you could get a good combo off. The more you age, the more damage you deal but the less health you have so go back to earlier missions so you can start later missions at a younger age and with the more you age the less moves you can learn so try learning what you think the best skills from the skill tree are before you get too old. If you find a jade dragon statue anywhere in the levels, you can use your xp, level score, or age to upgrade specific traits that you automatically gain like guard stamina and weapon durability or you can use the statues to upgrade your skill tree without having to be dead. Lastly, if you don’t do well on some of the bosses and die too much or die at all, you can go back to that boss faster through a shortcut with items found in later missions or earlier missions and then start learning their patterns. If anyone reads this, I hope you find this helpful. 

Edit: I forgot to say, hold circle after an opponent is laying on the ground for a couple of free punishes. It’ll allow you to literally dodge anything that’s coming towards you at the moment for some breathing room. Also thank you Cory and everyone else for the love on this comment. Much love ❤️❤️❤️!

I beat this game yesterday at 23 year old true ending. Here’s some tips for new players.

Focus enemies with damaged structure. In this vid Cory didn’t know but he barely executed anyone. The yellow bar is called structure and if someone’s structure is really damaged focus them first to get rid of them quickly.

Don’t get cornered. 

If you attack on the dialogue parts you will surprise them and be able to “execute them” instantly. So usually go for strongest opponents on dialogue parts.

Parrying is your best friend. (Blocking right before attack) as it breaks the opponents structure. You can sometimes execute bosses at 50% health with this strategy.

Fall damage as seen even in this video can be your worst enemy or your best friend. It’s easy to take out tons of enemies with it.

Exploring the levels is worth it because you can unlock shortcuts that sometimes go straight to the boss even so you can make a better run next time you try the level.

Have fun and keep a cool head. This game makes you feel like a total badass once you put a few hours into it. It’s so fun and really rewarding to learn it!

Cory, I want to give you some tips for you and anyone who play Sifu:
1. When you sweep your enemies, hold circle to attack them to lower their health and structure
2. When you hold your block button, you can use you left stick at the same time to dodge attacks, this being a stationary dodge and can help rebuild your structure when blocking and parrying.
3. When enemy limbs start to light up, those are unparryable attacks, and you want to dodge them, either using hold L1+ Left stick or pressing R2.
4. Each time you finish the level of the game, you stay that age for the next level. Finishing a level will give you passage to shortcuts to the boss, so you can die less and begin the next level at a younger age.
5. At the Wuguan (headquarters), there is a training area inside where the mission select table is. Go to the training dummy behind the table on the right, and you can train with an AI to help you practice your attacks, dodges, parrying etc.

Hopefully this helps you to not feel like a trash gamer on Sifu. This is a tough game, so button mashing is not a suitable strategy. Carefully timed commands will help you succeed

Alright, here's the endings I could find [NO SPOILERS]:

1: Freedom Ending:
To get this ending, you need to find the docking exit, it's located near the kitchen I believe. Use this exit to get the next ending.

2: Princess Quest Ending:
This one simply requires you to beat Princess Quest 2, then select the Vanny ending at the exit door, and once in Vanny's lair, complete Princess Quest 3. And BOOM! Another ending complete!

3: Emergency Ending:
[EDIT: You may be able to get this ending without all the Golden Plushies, but I'm not sure]
To get this ending, you need to exit through the emergency exit behind the prize counter; it's past El Chip's, and through the arcade. You need all 6 gold plushies to be able to reach it (although you've already gotten 2 of them).
Here's how to get the remaining 4:
Golden Chica: Enter the elevator in the food court, near the salad bar; this should lead to an abandoned cafeteria. On the right side of this area, you'll see some TV screens with some static, look behind the nearby counter, and there it is.
Golden Roxy: You'll need Monty's Claw upgrade for this one. Enter the utility tunnels near the beginning of the game. Start to go down the stairs for a bit until you see a gate with a cleaning robot behind it (you saw him in ep. 1), break through with Monty's claws, and there it is!
Golden Sun & Golden Moon: The moon is quite complicated, I lumped the sun here too since you can get him along the way. The first thing you'll need is the Faz-Cam from Monty Golf. There is actually 6 ending.
The first, bad ending, which has a one-star rating, requires you to simply exit the Pizzaplex through the front door at 6 AM. Gregory escapes alone, and it doesn’t end well for anybody.

The second, good ending, which has two stars, demands you to stay in the building and obtain a Level 7 Security pass. You can then go into the Loading Dock area through the ground floor kitchen and escape that way. Freddie and Gregory escape with in a van. It is a sweet ending, but doesn’t “solve” anything.

For Ending #3, Unmasked, you’ll need to upgrade Freddy with Roxy’s eyes. Then, when the clock strikes 6 AM, escape the Pizzaplex using the emergency exit at the Prize Counter area. You’ll escape to the roof, the place will start burning, and Freddy will save you from Vanny thanks to his new eyes.

The fourth and probably best of the FNAF Security Breach endings is also the true, canon ending. To get it, you’ll have to defeat Chica, Roxy and Monty and fully upgrade Freddy. Then, you use the Old Elevator to go down into the Old Pizzeria and a boss fight ensues. I won’t spoil what happens during and after said fight.

To get the fifth ending (aka Disassembled), you need to play Fazer Blast and discover Vanny’s lair above the arena. Then, as you approach the front door at 6 AM, select the “Vanny” option instead. Press the button in her lair and just follow what the game tells you. Again, not spoiling this one, as it is probably the most gruesome of the bunch.

The sixth and final ending is also the only three-start one. It requires you to complete two Princess Quest arcade games (one in Roxy’s Salon, one in the Arcade, where Music Man is). Then, when you get to an exit, choose the Vanny option, but instead of messing with the button, you can play and complete the third arcade in the villain’s lair. This triggers this ending, which is the trickiest to get.

First off, you'll need the Claw Upgrade from Monty before you can get this ending. Behind Roxy Raceway, there is a door with some broken fencing in front of it with "Caution: Restricted Area" signs on it. The door should say "Staff Only". through this door you'll come across a locked gate, usse Monty's claws to get behind this gate, and viola! You're on your way to the True Ending. Keep in mind, your game will auto-save before the final section of this ending, so it is recommended you make a second save slot before doing this ending!

4: Emergency Ending:
To get this ending, you need to exit through the emergency exit behind the prize counter; it's past El Chip's, and through the arcade. You need all 6 gold plushies to be able to reach it (although you've already gotten 2 of them).
Here's how to get the remaining 4:
Golden Chica: Enter the elevator in the food court, near the salad bar; this should lead to an abandoned cafeteria. On the right side of this area, you'll see some TV screens with some static, look behind the nearby counter, and there it is.
Golden Roxy: You'll need Monty's Claw upgrade for this one. Enter the utility tunnels near the beginning of the game. Start to go down the stairs for a bit until you see a gate with a cleaning robot behind it (you saw him in ep. 1), break through with Monty's claws, and there it is!
Golden Sun & Golden Moon: The moon is quite complicated, I lumped the sun here too since you can get him along the way. The first thing you'll need is the Faz-Cam from Monty Golf. Next, head to the daycare, if you go around edge of the daycare, you'll find a theater; in this theater, you'll see a poster for "Captain Foxy's Pirate Adventure", you'll need to find cutouts of the 4 characters on this poster and take pictures of them. For Foxy: there is a room with some cutouts in the theater itself; in the back of this room, you'll find the Foxy you're looking for, snap a pic, and his eye will glow. You'll know you're doing it right if their eyes glow. Next is Chica (she's a mermaid) & the Golden Sun: go to Kid's Cove, it's next to Monty Golf. There, open the door to the lighthouse, here you'll find the Golden Sun. In the same room on the other side, you should see the Chica cutout, snap a pic, make them eyes glow, then on to the next! Now for Bonnie: in the backroom corridor where the giant DJ Music Man was, travel to the end of the corridor where Princess Quest 2 is, right next to it you'll see Bonnie on his side. You know what to do at this point. And finally, Freddy: go the place where you got the Photo-Pass near the beginning of the game, and enter the door to the right of the Rockstar Freddy cutout. In this area, you'll need to find the rehearsal room, it should be in the top right section of this area if you look at your map. Upon entering the rehearsal room you'll see Freddy, snap the last pic, and leave. After all that's done, go back to the poster in the Daycare Theater, and you'll find a secret passage. You'll find a hallway that leads to a familiar room, but there is a secret room nearby with an arcade machine, this is the room that has the Golden moon Plush.
Now with all the golden plushies you can find the exit, as I said before: It's past El Chip's, and through the arcade; you'll find the exit behind the prize counter. Leave through the door and THE END! You got the last ending that is currently known.

The singing at 24:32 is actually a real person named Alessandro Moreschi who was the last Castrati recorded. Castrati were apart of choirs in the church back in the 16th century when women were still largely oppressed and couldn't participate in Church proceedings such as the Choir. Castrati were young, prepubescent boys who's testicles were removed before puberty (or castrated, simply, hence the name Castrati). This was done so that the boys could reach the high, soprano notes in church songs that an average man could not physically or musically reach. I know this is old but if you still like this series or you still don't quite get the story, here is the whole story wrapped up in a bow:

It started with us the scummy main character, Doug Houser. We neglected, verbally, and possibly physically abused his wife and his daughter. He apparently he had a side chick who happened to be his secretary. (fun fact: he is in sales for a big worldwide money management company so he is making bank) He promised to his side chick he would split up with his wife and then to get back at her, he would then take Tammy (his daughter). He couldn't split up with his wife because his wife wanted him to stay and wouldn't agree on a divorce because she wanted to have a 'normal' family for they're autistic daughter. Doug was introduced to the dark arts and Malak and Doug was going to make a deal with Malak for success and stuff, but he needed a sacrifice and chose to kill his wife and child by messing with the brakes. They drove over the bridge and lost control of the car, falling into the water. So now that Doug had success after the murders, he lived his life but then got sick with cancer, the secretary left him for around this time because she figured out he murdered them and he had major cancer so she wasn't having any of it so she dipped pretty quick for another rich man. Before Doug died, he wrote in his blood a pentagram, this was supposed to sacrifice his afterlife to Bierce and when he died, the beginning of the game started.
Malak in this story is supposed to be like the devil but more managemental, he owns a big worldwide 'company', he makes deals with both the living and the dead and of course there is always a price to pay and they get karma blah blah blah.

Now it's time for some Bierce lore! In the 1930s, Helen Bierce came from British descent, she came to Hollywood to become a popular actress, but was inexperienced so she married a rich man who had strong connections to the film industry, Edgar, but only for his money. Edgar stole movie costumes and performed fake satanic rituals with his friends for fun, eventually they invited a man from Hungary called Victor who came from a culture that strongly believed in dark magic. Bierce, running out of options on how to become a successful actress, turned to Victor for help. Bierce thought Victor could teach her about dark magic to get what she wanted, so she convinced him to mentor her. Victor rented out a flat and mentored Bierce for months until he taught her about a ritual on how to summon a demon called Malak: Sacrifice a person’s daughter and he will come and grant you a wish, it will last several years until he comes to get your soul as payment. Bierce did the ritual by sacrificing the daughter of a maid for the ritual, Malak came and would make her a successful actress in exchange for her soul after 7 years and a day. Bierce agreed, and the next day all the film studios were calling her to be in their movies, Victor disappeared, and after becoming a successful actress and getting what she wanted, Bierce poisoned her husband and inherited his wealth. Bierce didn't plan to stick to her deal with Malak, so she looked for a way to repel the demon. She learned of a ring called the Riddle of Heaven which could strip Malak's power away. She found it in a far away country, when Malak came to finish their deal. Bierce tried to suck away Malak's power with the ring. Bierce gained a bit of his power before he banished her between Heaven and Hell, but the ring created a pocket dimension which was in the middle of the afterlife. The ring fell into Hell and Bierce was stuck in a Ballroom pocket dimension which became a purgatory for souls who did both good and bad in their life. Personal Hells opened up between pillars in the pocket dimension, along with a gate way to Hell. The Riddle of Heaven appeared to be a giant alter which was shattered into pieces all over her personal Hells. She sent these souls into the portals to collect the shattered crystals (now being called "Soul Shards") to rebuild the altar to strip away what's left of Malak's power to become an actress and do whatever she wants. Malak created monsters to guard the Soul Shards which got most of the souls killed. However, Bierce's luck would turn when she comes across Doug Houser.

Anyway, all of the levels are based off of not only some minor references to Doug's past life, but all of the fears are Bierce's. The first level was based off of the day before he killed his family. Him and his secretary went to a hotel for a business trip and she said that there wouldn't be any "monkey business" * badum tss *. The second is both a mix of Bierce's and Doug's, Bierce wanted a child when she was still alive but she was unable to due to medical problems and Doug with his association with his daughter Tammy. The third with the statues is Bierce's fear of inanimate objects such as statues and the anxiety of something is behind her. The fourth is Bierce's, the fear of inflatables. The fifth is of course Bierce's which is the fear of clowns but also from her trauma of being a movie star. Torment therapy, level 6, was a about only Doug this time, It was his trauma and all he went through in the hospital before he died and basically of his nightmares and feelings. The reason why the nurses didn't have a head to symbolize the fact that when you are near death, you can't see people's faces. The reason why the nurses are major man haters is to represent how he sees himself as scum to woman because of what he has done. Mascot mayhem, the joy joy level, is supposed to represent the childlike innocence of his daughter and the mascots were supposed to be a reflection on how Doug behaved towards Tammy. The last level with Mama bear and the babies, they were supposed to represent the nightmare Doug has over his wife and his daughter, he feels like he wasn't good enough. Partially, this is also some other people's opinion, it could also represent how Bierce wished to have a family but was unable to with her life and etc.

It’s interesting how every level of the game ties into Doug’s backstory/personality flaws:

The monkey hotel is a reference to how his secretary told him “no monkey business”, and the reason it’s a hotel is because that’s where a lot of affairs tend to happen.

The school and Agatha are directly a reference to how Tammy (Doug’s daughter) died young.

The golden statue guys are a reference to Doug’s shallowness and greed (his wife mentions that he only cares about work, and he buys his secretary a bunch of stuff).

The circus might be a stretch, but I think it depicts how Doug sees himself as a “fool” for how he treated his family.

The ducks are about deception and pretending to be innocent even when they aren’t; Doug lies to his wife about the cheating and tries to act as if he has no fault in any of his problems. The ducks are also all broken toys, so it may represent how Doug called his wife and daughter “defective”.

The nurses are all likely a reference to Doug’s infidelity, but they are also hospital themed; Doug is currently stuck in a hospital bed.

Joy Joy land is obvious; Doug told his family that they were “sucking the joy” out of his life.

The mama bear may be a stretch, but I think it hints that Doug had an abusive mother, which would explain why he treats his own family so horribly.

So basically, this game is an entire metaphor for McDonnel's sins, and the nun is her alter-ego. The mission to rescue the child is actually a quest to become good again. Because children represent innocence. The Good Ending is where you burn her and the clown says "You are forgiven" which means you are given a second chance at life, and to become a better person.
The Bad Ending is where you fall in a narrow pit, then the nun creeps up and slowly fills the pit with her "acidic" vomit. Completely makes no sense.
The Ending where you are stuck in a reality-bending vent and a lil light figure comes at you and kills you is...The IDK Ending.
The Neutral Ending is you collect all body parts and put them all on the scale, get the gear from inside the scale and put it on the clock. A secret passage will open, this will give you a candle I think. then you go to the floor with all the lockers, find rubbing alcohol, find the crate with rope tied on it, and burn it with the alcohol. Then find the code and enter it on a certain locker, and you will get the second candle, then you find a prayer room, put the candles in, then the glass frame bursts and there will be a corpse hung on a cross, it has a stone head attached on it. Take the head, go to the graveyard, put the head on the headless statue, then the ground will open up. Read the letter, go inside the hole, close the coffin, bam. neutral ending. AKA the hardest ending to get. Basically McDonnel goes insane and buries herself alive.

If y'all want the lore here:

Basically, before the events in the game, Ms. Mcdonald had sent her atheist daughter to a strict and abusive boarding school so that she can conform into her christianity, and all while doing this, Ms. Mcdonald kept convincing herself that she isn't a monster if she doesn't cause the harm but rather let the others do it. So then Jamie (the daughter) had been horrifically bullied by the other kids at the school and abused by the nuns, especially Sister Aplonia. Bongo, a doll that her mother had given Jamie, was the only friend she actually had. And so soon, Jamie had hung herself, causing the school to shut down to a lot of rumors about the whole incident occuring. Ms. Mcdonald becomes ridden with absolute guilt, because she was the one who forced Jamie into an abusive school and she was the indirect cause of her suicide. And after a few years of grieving, Ms. Mcdonald goes insane, going back to the abandoned school, and imagining that she had received a letter, to which she actually didn't. The nun that chases down is the manifestation of Jamie in the mother's mind, bitter and angry, seeking vengeance for what her mother did. And her appearance is based on a nun from the 1800s who got her eyes taken out by the romans, but allegedly, Christ had saved her and cleaned her soul free of them. As you go around the school, you realize that all the notes you see are written from Jamie, or what her mother think she would have wrote. And the doll that is hanging is Bongo, another manifestation of Jamie's suicide.

Bad Ending: Jamie doesn't forgive her mother for what she did, and decides to cleanse her soul.

Neutral: Ms. Mcdonald cannot handle the grief and guilt she has anymore so she decides to bury herself in a coffin inside the school so she can burn in hell.

Good: Ms. Mcdonald gets rid of the manifestation of the nun, symbolizing that she is sorry, and that she will forever never forgive herself but rather, getting rid of Jamie's tormenters would appease her mind. That's why when you click on Bongo, it says "you are forgiven" because Jamie forgives her mother for indirectly causing her death, and thus lets her go in peace since her mother gotten rid of the tormentors and had come all this way for it.

Overall, Ms. Mcdonald is a shitty mother for sending her daughter to an abusive environment just for her religious beliefs to be conformed into Jamie and Jamie deserved better, and the good ending somewhat helps that.

When you realize the small “nun” at the end of the game was the main characters daughter, Janie, that the real nun, Mother Apolonia, trapped and disguised as herself 👀 The main character burned her child alive. 
Some replies have made me realize further evidence of this: 
-When the player tries to interact with the small nun (I'll just call her Janie to avoid confusion) the prompt they receive is "Don't believe her lies". I believe this is the player's (i.e., the mother's) internal dialog reacting to Janie, undoubtedly trying to get her mom to listen to her, to save her. But after this entire ideal of desperately trying to escape with her life from Mother Apolonia, the mother is too blinded by fear and trauma to realize that its her own daughter in front of her, and rationalizes it by saying "Don't believe her lies". 
-kind of obvious, but the fact that Janie was that height in the first place. Mother Apolonia was consistently shown to be taller that the player. For the devs to make such an obvious mistake in the characters model at the climax of the story is impossible. 
-the fact that Janie is caged. Through the notes found by the player, we discover that Mother Apolonia was abusive and cruel to her "students", giving them inhumane punishments for the smallest of mistakes. It seems realistic that Mother Apolonia would imprison Janie in a cage, even dress her as a nun herself as some sort of punishment. Why in the world would Mother Apolonia be in a cage? Especially after just being seen throughout the building?
-Bongo the Clown. One of the letters says that bongo is Janie's toy, and that she hid it from the Nun so she wouldn't take it away. The fact that its hanging outside her cage, just beyond her reach, makes me think it was hung there by Mother Apolonia as another punishment upon its discovery. 
There's even more evidence, like the noise Janie makes, which is more of a whimper, a sound that Mother Apolonia has never made, or the fact that the story ends without actually "finding" Janie, which was the whole point.

Rocks - can be to distract the Nun and also to break the glass.
Pistol - using pistol won't exactly kill the Nun, but will cause her to run away, giving the player more time.
Radar - can be used to detect the Nun's movement.
Screwdriver - can be used to unscrew bolts from the vent cover.
Hammer - can be used for removing nails from wooden planks that have been used to barricade the door.
VHS tapes - can be inserted into VHS players at certain locations.
Lighter - primary light source.
Wire clipper - can be used for cutting wires.
Notes - written by children, can be found in many rooms.
Wooden plank - can be used to walk across the barbed wire pit.
Bandages - can be used to heal wounds.
Mannequin parts - can be found scattered all over the school. Can be placed on the scale.
Drain cleaner - can be poured in the specific drain, dislodging the hex key that was in the drain.
Gear - can be placed in a clock.
Hex Key - For unlocking a certain white door.

"How did he forget that???" Scientifically speaking, it's a trauma response. Your brain can literally delete (or just reallyy try to forget) traumatic memories as a way of protecting itself.
This game is a masterpiece, best written one that ive ever seen. Just a clusterfuck of twists.

27:00 Cory, basically when someone goes through something traumatic, their brain can literally suppress the memory so deep that they forget it ever happened. It’s not because it wasn’t a big deal—it’s actually the opposite. The brain’s just trying to protect them, like, “Nah, this is too much, let’s lock it away for now.” And for a while, it works. You live life thinking you’re fine, but then something random triggers it, and the memory comes back outta nowhere. A sound, a smell, a certain place can hit you and suddenly it’s like, “Wait, where did that come from?” That’s why some people feel anxious or off and don’t know why. It’s the trauma still living in the background. Remembering it doesn’t mean anything’s wrong with you—it just means something finally shook it loose. So yeah, forgetting something painful isn’t weird—it’s survival mode.

The “Listen Ending” is actually the beginning of the timeline of events. These 2 people meet, date, get married and are about to have a baby. For all they know they’re strangers. The husband comes home and then the conversation plays out, the wife goes to the bathroom to get the watch and then suggest going out on a walk. Now on their walk she shows the husband the watch and tells her past. How she ran from home and she tells him she’s pregnant. Since she’s pregnant she wants to visit home and reconnect with her dad.
They both end up going to do this and all the normal stuff like introduce her new husband and inform the dad about the baby but instead the dad realizes the husband is actually his son. Which leads into the talking scenes in the library.

Fun fact: Six and Mono are named after which concept art drawing they were. Mono was first (mono means one), and Six was the 6th. The creators thought of using the numbers, and just rolled with it. 

Another fun fact (spoiler for video ending!): It's confirmed by the creators of the game that Six dropped Mono because she recognized him.

For anyone wondering why Six dropped Mono it wasn’t because she was evil. Back in Chapter 4 of Little Nightmares II, when the Thin Man comes out of the TV, Six and Mono try to hide under the bed. Only Mono makes it out, and the Thin Man ends up taking Six, tearing her soul apart. You can actually see this later after the train crash, there’s a shadow of Six, a piece of her soul that’s still a little playful.
When Mono destroys the music box the only thing that gave Six comfort and let her escape from the horrible world they’re stuck in he also destroys her last bit of peace. With her soul shattered and full of negative emotions, she lets him fall.
That’s what creates the time loop. Mono falls, becomes the Thin Man, and his younger self goes through everything all over again. The only way the cycle could ever be broken is if Six had chosen to save him.
So, in the end, Six didn’t drop Mono out of cruelty she did it because she wasn’t whole anymore. The Thin Man had already taken the part of her that was hopeful and kind, and when the music box was destroyed, the last thing keeping her together was gone.

Watching Cory go through all 5 stages of grief following the betrayal is such an experience lmao. Denial, anger, bargaining, depression, acceptance— he goes through all of it basically in that exact order 💀💀

Never run across glass. As you saw in the vid it bleeds you and hurts a lot so either walk or crouch walk across untill you have shoes.

If she is in her killer mode she lock you in a room with her and count to 5 and than come after you, if you get close to her while she is counting she will just outright stab you like you seen in the video.
If you have a key she will say things like "Come here" or "give me that key" and  she will reach out with her hand asking for it. If you get close to her when she asks for it she will knock you down, take the key and put it in a different room.

Fun Fact: Aka Manto is a Japanese spirit or Yokai that lurkes around school toilets.

When a student goes inside and finishes, they will realise that there is no toilet paper.
A voice will then ask what colour toilet paper they want (the different paper sheet colours in game) depending on what sheet they pick depends on what grim fate awates them.
Red: Killed brutally with a knife or sucked down the pipes
Blue: Strangled or has all fluids sucked out of their body.
Purple: You could possibly survive
Yellow: drowned in your own pee
(don't know any more of them)
If you pick a colour not in the selection, you will die.
If you say "I don't need any paper" you have a chance to escape if fast enough .
If you bring toilet roll to the bathroom to cheat the system, then your paper disappears and have to answer anyway. 
Those who mension their encounter with the Aka Manto will get dragged into the Nether World for eternity.

Another part of the Japanese urban legend is that it usually appears in girl bathrooms and not just any bathroom. 

Ako Manto is a unknown entity that appears to students in the bathroom when they are alone and offers them red toilet paper or blue toilet paper. If you choose red, they will be lacerated to the point that their dead body is drenched in their own blood. If you choose blue, you either get strangled or all the blood is drained from your body. If you try to outsmart it saying a different color such as green or orange, you will be dragged to hell for your soul to burn. In some variations of the myth if you choose yellow you will be drowned in the toilet. It doesn’t allow you to run away since it simply blocks the exit and the only way to get it to go away is to kindly refuse the paper or ignore it. This also explains why there was writing on one of the stalls saying “Red paper? Blue paper?”

Here’s some tips: Jimmy can’t hide in the basement, ground floor, elevator or the stairwell. So these places are safe zones.

The menu in the right corner might change color, if it turns red, it means he is following you or he knows where you are.

You can call for Jimmy in the top left. It might be good for strategy. You can maybe trap him in a room using a dead lock key. Example if you call out to Jimmy when your in a room, wait till Jimmy starts to open the door thats when you want to hide in the closet, once you do that Jimmy will now go in the bathroom and hide. Thats when you want to run out the room and use the dead lock key. It will not trap him forever but it gives you time to look around. If your going on the steps and you happen to see Jimmy peak through the door/ window do NOT go through the door. 

Jimmy will take some time before spawning on the floors, he will spawn quicker on floor 3 than floor 1. Every time you complete the story more he will spawn faster. When you reach about 70% of the story, he will spawn instant on 1 - 3!

So, if your searching for a room it is a good idea to go back to the elevator, then go down to ground floor. Then go back to the floor you are tryna find the room. If you do that, the timer for Jimmy to spawn will reset. Then you have extra time to look. (This is useless if you are at 70%, because he will spawn instant). You can see if he has spawned be calling for him in a room. If it takes too long for him to appear, that means he hasn’t spawned yet.

Audio is also an important part of the game, listen carefully for footsteps when you look through the spyglass in the guest rooms.

Tips for Cory: For starters, the Ground Floor and the Stairway both count as safety points where Jimmy will not hunt you down, so you are safe in these areas. However in the stairwell, sometimes when you turn around to look back at the door, you will see Jimmy look in the door way and back off,  so DO NOT go out the door because he will get you. Use the Scrying Mirror to look for clues on where to go to next or what to put together to progress further. If you ask the right questions and put the right things together, the story will start to make even more sense. You left off where Jimmy poured some type of liquid on the teddy bear, which is connected to the Turpentine and Lighter, so you have to ask Amy about those two things. As the story goes on and you’re done with Amy, there will be a second spirit that you have to figure out what happened to. 

For keys, when you have the deadlock keys for certain rooms, you could also lock yourself in there when you know Jimmy is looking for you, but you can also trap Jimmy inside the rooms as well. To know if you’re in danger, at the bottom right of the screen, the menu(i think that’s what it is) will change certain colors, red meaning you are in extreme danger, so watch out for that. 

In a dark room and you know Jimmy is looking for you, you can hide in the bathroom and run out as he walks further into the room and lock him inside of the room. In a lit up room, you have to have Jimmy see you hide in the wardrobe and that will prompt him to hide in the bathroom which gives you a chance to also run out of the room and lock him in there. You can also look through the key hole in doors so you can see if he is in certain rooms hiding to get you. If Jimmy looks at the peephole, wardrobes, and bathrooms for a long amount of time, it’s a high possibility that he knows you’re in there and will back off to get you secretly.

EDIT: After looking at some other gameplays, the second character and Amy are somewhat connected- you can ask the second character about things you’ve found out about Amy which will also let you progress. When you ask questions and ask the right one, you will also hear a sparkling kind of noise that indicates you’re on the right path as well. And with the locked doors, Jimmy can STILL get inside, so you still have to hide when he turns the doorknobs.

On Wednesday, Osana and Senpai have a conversation on where the best spot is to relax. Osana will prove that she can get a better spot for him. At lunchtime, before Osana goes to the Rooftop, you must fill a bucket of water and put it on top of the door as a trap. Then she'll go to the locker rooms change. On Thursday, Osana is going to ask Senpai to on a date with her after school. After school around four in the afternoon, Osana will go to the roof and take a little nap, setting an alarm to wake herself up so she can meet senpai. Once you complete it, it will turn off her alarm, causing her to oversleep and miss the date with Senpai

On Friday, Osana and Senpai will talk about what type of music they listen to. At lunchtime, Osana is going to put together a playlist for Senpai to show him the music she listens too. Then return Osana's phone to her desk before lunchtime. During lunchtime, Senpai will get a bit angry that she made him listen to this.

- Before you file the last report of the night, double check all the windows. If there are any unlocked, or any lights out, cue ball will get into the house during the night.

Some Tips to counter enemies (I know someone else said it but saying just to say it no need to like)

Doctor: Don’t waste your time checking the windows unless the lights are turned off in that  area. If you keep checking every window, you leave yourself vulnerable to the doctor as you need to always check the cameras for he comes. You should always check your camera from time to time at a reasonable interval as you read your reports. Use your sense of hearing to listen for noises and remembered flash the lights when you spot him outside 

Steve Austin: ALWAYS lock all the windows at the start of a night, and don’t keep checking for every window UNLESS YOU HEAR THE SOUND OF CRICKETS OR ANYTHING. That means your window is unlocked/opened. Always take a look at the windows in a room where the lights turned off. That’s where most likely the windows are open 

General tips 
-always use your flashlight when the lights are off, it’s pretty important so you know which windowed are unlocked 
-set yourself a timer to check for cameras. Checking ever 30 seconds or minute and cut that time down if On later nights 
-when In doubt, open your closets. It helps you hide from Steve Austin giving you a stunner when your lights are closed, it’s also great so you know where the killers are possibly hiding in because you can tell if the doors closed 
-never underestimate the sound signals the game gives you if you heat footsteps or a car pass by,always take a look at your cameras, then dismount from the PC to take a look and see if any lights are shut off 
 
Good luck and I have something to tell you your next video might include a save file

Quick Tips: 
1. Tanner: When you see "Tanner" in the cameras (the guy with white clothes) you need to flash him DIRECTLY in his face when he gets close to the camera. (Shining light on him from his left or right doesn't work, so switch cams to the direction he is running in and flash.) It makes him go away, but you might trip the breaker if you have the light turned on fro too long. (The breaker is in the file room closet). If he appears behind a wall and disappears (the corridor) DO NOT open the door next to the main door. (Keep it open at the start and if it's closed at some point Tanner's in there. Tips to counter the enemies

Tanner aka Doctor the guy at the cameras: Don't waste your time checking the windows unless the lights turn off in that area. If you keep checking every window, you leave yourself vulnerable to the doctor as you need to always check the cameras for whenever he comes. You should always check your cameras from time to time at a reasonable interval as you read your reports. Use your sense of hearing to check for noises and remember to flash the lights when you spot him outside.

Steve Austin the guy who is bald: Always lock all windows at the start of the game, and don't keep checking for every window unless you hear the sound of crickets and cicadas noises outside. That sound means your window is open/unlocked. Always take a look at the windows in a room where the lights have been turned off. Most probably those are the spots where the windows opened again. 

General Tips

- Always use your flashlights when the lights are off, it's pretty important so you know which windows have been unlocked.
- Set yourself a timer to check for the cameras. Checking every 30 secs or a minute seems fine enough, you'll have to increase the frequency as time goes by.
- When in doubt, open your closets. It helps you hide from Steve Austin giving you a stunner when your lights are closed. It's also great so you know where the killers are possibly hiding in because you can tell if they closed the doors.
- Never underestimate the sound signals the game gives you. If you hear footsteps or a car passing by, always take a look at your cameras, then dismount from the PC to take a look and see if any lights are shut off.
-Middle mouse button for the curtains to open/close.

Tips For Enchantments Cory:

For beginning enchanting, you would really want to enchant pretty much only these items in the early enchanting with these enchantments below. 

Sword: 

Sharpness: (recommended) Does a general amount of more damage to all mobs. Good to start off with.

Unbreaking: Makes the durability of your item last longer.

Looting (Optional, but use this if found no matter what) Increased mob loot drops when they are killed (Use for endermen, you will thank me)

Pickaxe:

Efficiency: (recommended) Increases speed of how fast blocks are mined.

Unbreaking: Makes the durability of your item last longer.

Fortune: (Optional, but use this if found no matter what) Increases drops of coal, redstone,  lapis, and  most importantly DIAMONDS.

All Armor: (helmet, chest plate, leggings, and boots)

Protection: (Very Recommended) Best general defense that you should always get. Protects you from mostly all damage done to you.

Unbreaking: Makes the durability of your item last longer.

These are really what you only need at your point of the game. When you defeat the Ender Dragon, (last main quest) you get at least over 50 levels of experience. After you defeat the dragon, (hopefully) i will tell you ever single enchantment when you are ready. You should also surround your enchantment table with atleast 15 bookshelves, 1 block away from the table.

NOTE: THE HIGHER THE LEVEL OF THE ENCHANTMENT, THE MORE EFFECTIVE IT IS.
ex. Sharpness II > Sharpness I

(Tip: I see you have enchanted your sword with Bane of Arthropods. That is not very good unless you plan on only really killing spiders and silver fish. You can make a grind stone (2 wood planks, 2 sticks, 1 stone slab) And put your sword in there. That way, you can re enchant it with sharpness.

So for those who don't understand "Knock Knock" I'll explain it for you in the best way possible. So basically in the video you can see that the woman lives next to her neighbor with 4 kids and in the drama she seems very abusive to her children, at the end you see the children locked in the freezer and she starts screaming at them, so let's break this down. So how do I say this, well, there's only one house. The character displayed in the video is schizophrenic. Those children are actually her children, she doesn't have a twin house, it's just one house. She killed the children and in her imagination she still believes they are all there. When she enters the "second house" which is her house, she opens the freezer up to see 2 of her dead children, which are the children she killed, and she gets a terrifying realization, that those are her children, that it's her house, which is why she starts singing, and then eventually the other side of her awakens. And as you can see at 13:47 she's banging on the freezer, yelling at the "children", which are dead. She cooks food and leaves it at her porch to bring her satisfaction thinking she's helping the kids in the other house. The child you see running around in the footage of her upstairs, is her dead child taunting her. Basically, shes both the abusive
 mother and the neighbor, but she didn't have the ability to comprehend it until she saw her children were dead. The child you saw asking "Why" when she walked down the stairs was her the ghost of her child asking why she killed them. The water you saw she touched that turned in to blood represented the melted ice from the freezer and the blood that was shed when she killed them. When she heard them being hit and the vase shattering, it was a memory in the past of when she killed them, but which still haunts her, but she does not have the ability to comprehend it. The good neighbor trying to help them is actually a voice in her head. Summary, there is no good neighbor trying to help the children in the other house, there are no children, there is only one house, it's all in her imagination, This is actually based off of a true story and is very sad, if i'm not mistaken, i believe she called the cops to address the situation but then after research they find out it's her. Tips:
-Crouch so you dont fall in caves or off of things etc
- Your shield will eventually break
-"The village guardian" is an iron golem and it will attack you if you harm a villager
-The mobs with crossbows are called pillagers and they raid villages.
-Turn your coordinates on to help you if you get lost
- Craft a compass to better direct you to spawn
- You can steal leashes from wandering traders by killing them or the llamas, leashes can be attached to any animal to help guide them or take them with you such as when you're  gathering farm animals or bringing along a dog.
- Milk can be used for when you are poisoned to make it go away
-If You ever get caught on fire use cobblestone etc and jump on top of it to put the fire out
-You can also gather and use villagers, to breed them you just give them potatoes
- Creepers are scared of cats
- You can make your own iron golem(s) to protect your house
- The marshes are where you can find mushrooms, witches and slimes
-Slimes can be killed and used to make sticky pistons
- There are different types of villages including one that is made completely out of snow
- If you travel enough in a desert you may find a temple DO NOT break the purple center block, you will fall directly down onto a pressure plate that will trigger tnt and blow you up. Dig 2 blocks to the side either direction, you can go straight down. There Will be 4 chests inside and you are able to loot all the chests. I would recommend destroying the pressure plate because a dropped item can trigger it as well. You can take the tnt too if you want.
- If you ever go in the ocean and a dolphin is swimming around you, follow it because it might lead you to a wrecked ship that could have good loot inside. You can also feed dolphins with raw cod.
- If you're in the ocean and you see a building in the water dont go in there because you arent prepared yet. You will die. 
- While in the ocean if a sound plays and a mob goes across your screen, row your boat AWAY. The mob is a Guardian fish and they will kill you with ease if you dont know what you're doing.
 Thats all i can think of for now, I hope you use this :)

Yo Cory. the big dude in the village is called an iron golem. they protect the villagers from hostile mobs like zombies and others! lemme list some more tips I got for you.

*Always carry a water bucket.* ESPECIALLY WITH LAVA
there's something you can do if you fall from high places which are placing water down right before you land. you can also climb water! it works as a cheap ladder. just remember to pick the water right up after placing and jumping in it, on your way down.
*don't be dramatic with the torches* 
why I say this is cuz I see that u got a fear of mobs spawning everywhere. but only place them if necessary. the mobs will not spawn in between two torches that are like 5 blocks apart. I'd suggest adding them like every 10 blocks. or when it too dark for you to see.

*mining* 
diamonds are the best minerals to use for tools. they are around Y: 16 (16 blocks above bedrock aka the lowest you can dig) and can be found near red stone and lava. I'd suggest you make a diamond pickax and sword/ax depending on the way you attack (since the ax has more damage than a sword when you jump).

*get around* 
Press F3 on your keyboard for coordinates, biome, light level, etc. These are VERY helpful for getting back home although I already know you fine with that. Just in case, write down your home coordinates if you don't know how to get back.

*PETS!!!!* 
Here ill tells you which animals you can make pets and how to make them your pets. BTW if you want to name them you must make an anvil and name tag then put the name tag in the anvil and RENAME the name tag then put the name tag on the desired pet. sounds confusing but it's pretty easy to do. also, do this after you tame the animal.
Horses: You must use apples to tame the horse. to know when you've tamed it, you keep giving it apples until red hearts show up around it. After you've tamed the horse. you cannot ride it unless you have a saddle. so don't just expect it to move with you after you've tamed it.
Wolf/dogs: Instead of apples you use bones!! you keep on giving it bones until the red hearts show up. after that, it's yours. it'll follow you and will teleport if far away (unless you set it down) and it also comes with a little collar on it! you can change it with a dye I believe.
Cats: These spawn in villages and jungles. Its basically the as the wolf but instead of bones you use fish to tame it!! you can also make it sit down.
Parrots: You can tame a parrot by giving it any kind of seeds such as melon seeds, seeds, pumpkin seeds, or beetroot seeds. You can set it down or it will just follow you around. they spawn in jungle biomes

Hey Cory, here's some few tips

- Diorite isn't really valuable it's only a decorative block and it's like Andesite and Granite

- Those guys you fought with a banner and crossbows are "Pillagers." They raid villages and can spawn randomly around you. If you kill the guy with the banner he'll give you a "Bad Omen affect" which would cause a village raid. That would be bad.

- To get rid off any potion buff or debuff like the poison you got from that spider, you need to drink Milk

- Talking about poison spiders, they can only spawn from spawners which is the block surrounded by the webs. They are a special type of spider that gives you poison when you get hit.

- Your shield can block explosions and any attack when you block with right click. It can even block creeper explosions which is that green mob enemy that you find in caves or at night.

- For farming, you want to make sure that you don't jump on the tilled ground, doing so would make it untilled and you have to till the block again

- Sugarcane cannot be placed on tilled ground. It can only be placed on grass or sand that's touching water.

- The wandering trader that you met can only trade if you give him Emeralds, which are villager currency. Emeralds can be obtained by trading with a villager that you find in a village.

- To reproduce any animal, you must have two of that same animal and give it the food that it likes. Sheep like Wheat, Cows like Wheat, Chickens like Wheat Seeds, and Pigs like Carrots.

- To get more wheat seeds, you can break grass that comes from grass blocks. To get Carrots and Potatoes, you have to find a Village somewhere in the world.

- When you are trying to craft, you can search for the item

- You can get a full set of Iron Armor, Iron tools, an Anvil to repair tools, and a shield with a stack of Iron Ore

- A stack of blocks are 64 of a certain item

- Coal burns 8 items at a time, so say you have 3 coal, it'll burn only 24 items

- When you cut down a tree make sure that you cut down all of the wood, this way you can get Apples and Tree Saplings.

- Apples are found from Oak Trees and Dark Oak Trees 

- This one is complicated: So Cory, there are different types of biomes and there are many. Some biomes are called: Plains, Forest, Deep Forest, Mountains, Ice Spike, Beaches, Flower Forest, Mushroom Island, Sea, Deep Sea, Coral Reef and more. Each biome has its own traits, such as Forests have Oak Trees and Birch Trees. Mushroom Islands are rare but once you find them enemies cannot spawn on them and they provide Mooshroom Cows which can give you infinite food called Soup. To get that infinite food it's the same as milking a cow but with a bowl and a Mooshroom Cow. Anyways, Ice Spike biomes have Ice Spikes, Snow, Ice, and Polar bears.

- Also, there are 3 different mob types, Passive, Neutral, and Hostile.
Passive mobs will not cause you harm such as cows, horses, chicken and so forth. Neutral mobs are first passive but if you hurt them they can become hostile. Such as wolves, spiders when it's daytime or in a lit up area, and Enderman (I'll explain that one in the next tip). Hostile mobs are aggressive towards you and will attack you no matter what, Creepers, Skeletons, and Zombies are prime examples.

- Enderman are neutral mobs that won't harm you, unless you attack them or stare at them. But Enderman are very important, they have a chance to drop Enderpearls which are important to the game. Although be careful, when Enderman attack you, you get hurt a lot. They are fast and can teleport away and around you. You can counter this by going under a two block only space since Enderman are 3 blocks tall.

- Phantoms can spawn if you don't go to sleep at night in your bed. They spawn when you don't go to sleep for three days straight and they spawn in the sky and fly down to attack you. As long as you stay inside you can't get hurt by them but once you see them I advise you to go to sleep so that they don't spawn for another three days. They also drop Phantom Membrane which can be made into a Potion

- Finally, when you mine, the ores that you want the most are in order from most important to least: Diamond, Gold, Iron, Lapis Lazuli, Redstone, and Coal. Emeralds can be found but they're hard to get because they only generate in the High Mountains biome. Diamond can be used to make armor and tools, Gold is mainly used for Gold apples, God Apples, Golden Carrots, Golden Nuggets, and Golden Watermelon. Iron is used to make armor and tools which are needed to get Diamond, Gold, Redstone and Emeralds. Lapis Lazuli is primarily used for enchanting to increase your amor and tools effectiveness and improve them. Redstone can be used for Minecraft Technology, which are Lamps, Machines like Pistons, Dispensers, Redstone Torches and more. But dealing with Redstone can be complicated. Coal is used for fuel, torches, and trading with Villagers, but not Wandering Traders. And lastly Emeralds are used for trading with Villagers

Cory, here are some tips: (Everyone please like this so Cory can get this info)
1. The "enemy fortress" is called a mineshaft. In mineshafts you can find lots or iron ore, minecarts with chests inside, and spawners. Spawners look like little cages with a little fire around them. To stop a spawner from spawning mobs, simply place a torch on top. You can see what the spawner will spawn if you look inside of the little cage. If you break a spawner, it will not drop. It will simply disappear.
2. The creatures in your thumbnail are known as Pillagers. They hold crossbows that will shoot at you, similar to skeletons. When you kill a certain amount of pillagers, you will get a bad omen effect. This will show in the top right of your screen. When you have this effect, do not visit villages. This will cause a raid to happen, which will spawn a bunch of pillagers to attack you and the villagers. To get rid of the bad omen effect, or any negative effect, simply right click on a cow with a bucket in your hand. this will cause the bucket to fill with milk, which you can drink by holding right click, similar to eating food. This, as I said earlier, will get rid of any negative effects.
3. The food that you can cook is any type of meat that an animal drops, as well as fish.
4. Diorite, Granite and Andesite have no use other than as decoration blocks.
5. If you double click the location to the right of the magnifying glass on a crafting table, you can search for items to make by typing them in.
6. If you see multiple wood/stone/sand structures, it could be a village. Villages hold villagers, whom you can trade with. There are many types of villagers, from farmers to armor-smiths. In some villager's houses there can also be chests. In these chests, you can find food, blocks, ore, and other useful items. Right click on a villager to trade with it.
7. If you mix lava and water, you get obsidian. When you get obsidian, it can only be mined with a diamond pickaxe. When you have 14 obsidian, make a rectangle of 4 obsidian on the ground horizontally, then 5 high on the 2 corners, and another 4 at the top. Make sure there is a 6 block hole in the middle. Then light it using flint and steel. To make flint and steel, you need 1 iron and 1 flint. You can get flint by mining gravel with a shovel.
Edit 1:
1. You can leave the 4 corners off of nether portals - From @gamatee
2. Right click if you make a map to map out your land - From @Ember Mars
3. You can breed the cows if you get another one. After you lure another one into the fence, feed 1 wheat to each cow and they will breed. You can breed almost any animal, but the breeding items are different for different animals

Some quick tips (LIKE SO CORY CAN SEE)


1. The group of "Pirates" are actually Pillagers
They come in groups, and if you find their outpost and kill their leader, you will get the bad omen effect. 
If you walk into a village with this effect a raid will start. These are a bit difficult to complete but with the right equipment, you get a lot of valuable items in the end. 
(Emeralds, enchantment books, Totem of Undying)


2. The "enemy fortress" is actually an abandoned mineshaft
These are rare, and if you keep exploring the mineshaft you will find loot within chests. You can also take the rails from the floor to make a transportation system. 
The cave spiders in the shafts can poison you. To get the poison effect off drink a bucket of milk. Destroy the black box at 16:45 for the cave spiders to stop spawning.


3. Villages
If you venture off into any direction, eventually you will find a village. Within the villages will be different types of villagers that you can trade with at the expense of emeralds. Some villages have iron golems. DO NOT HIT THEM AS THEY CAN EASILY KILL YOU. They are there to protect the villagers and will fight any mob that is harmful to you or the villagers. 


4. Bonemeal
If you put the bones you've been getting into a space in the crafting table, you should make 3 bonemeal. You can make crops grow faster with bonemeal.


5. Breeding 
Once you get 2 of each animal, you can begin breeding them for food. 
Cows take wheat to breed. Pigs take carrots to breed.
Chickens take seeds to breed and sheep take wheat to breed. 
You need to give the breeding item to BOTH animals for them to breed. So 2 wheat for 2 cows to breed. 


6. Riding a horse
Once you tame a horse you can ride it at much faster speeds than running, and it won't take hunger away.
To tame a horse keep right-clicking on it until hearts come out of it and it stops kicking you off it. In order to actually control the horse's movement, you need a saddle. You get these from chests or near mob spawners that are found within the mineshaft (enemy fortress) you found. 


7. Wandering Trader
He has somewhat a collection of rare items that you can trade if you have emeralds. If you kill his Llamas you will get lead, which can be used on animals like a leash (especially horses). 


Good Luck!

*_Minecraft Stuff:_*
Hey Cory! Here's an extended comment on some tips to do in Minecraft! 

Hey guys, make sure your information is correct! Especially when it comes to Minecraft versions! Java and Bedrock are different versions of Minecraft! Bedrock is Minecraft on mobile, console and Windows ten. Java is "the classic" version of Minecraft that is on PC. 

- For example, SHIELDS DON'T BLOCK IF YOU CROUCH IN JAVA, YOU GOTTA HOLD RIGHT CLICK! CORY IS PLAYING JAVA MINECRAFT!

- First off, it is highly recommended that you install Optifine for Minecraft! It allows for better FPS and the ability to tweak more video settings to your liking. It also allows you to do certain things and have access to features that greatly improve your Minecraft experience!

- Cory, turn on dynamic lighting in your video settings! It let's you hold torches to give out a light source without having to place them down! (Requires Optifine)

- Press "C" or whatever bind you're using to zoom in. Like you're using binoculars. (Optifine Only)

- *_turn off auto-jump (It's in controls)_*

— Sugar cane can only be placed next to a water source, they don't need to be placed on farmland either. The water source needs to be on the same level as the adjacent block. The block next to it has to be grass, dirt or sand. 
 
- Pillager patrols, (those gray bois w/crossbows) will spawn randomly. Killing the one with a banner above its head will give you "bad omen" status effect. Just be careful when you visit a village and you have the effect...

- Hit F3 in order to see your Minecraft's debug stats. These are important to see your coordinates to locate your position.

- Mining is important in Minecraft, go down to the y coordinates 10-13 to have the highest chance of finding diamonds and caves.

- Place torches on the left side when traversing caves or mineshafts (those underground wooden structures with those cave spider spawners that give you poison). Placing torches on the left means that it'll be easier to find your way back to the surface, this is because torches will be on the right side of each cave if your travelling back up.

- If you see a mob spawner (those blue cages with a spinning mob inside them), either place torches on them or destroy them with a pickaxe to stop them from spawning!

- Spiders are passive during the day! 

- Cobwebs are easier to cut with a sword.

- Axes do more damage than swords, however, they take longer to charge up for a stronger attack. 

- *_Shields can block explosions!_*

- Pressing F1 hides your hud, combining this with the "cinematic camera" option in controls allows you to take some cinematic shots of your Minecraft world! 

- Craft more than one furnace, it makes it easier to smelt/cook multiple things at a time.

- Different flowers make different dyes! Use can use these to dye your bed or leather armor different colours. 

- Eat to heal! You won't quick-heal if you're hungry!

- Some Mobs can give you different effects, drink buckets of milk in order to negate any effect you have. e.g. Poison, Blindness and Nausea. 

- Villages and Outposts: Villages appear randomly around the world, they contain villagers who can be traded with for items and tools. Villages also contain farms and food stockpiles which can be looted to your desire. Outposts are usually dangerous structures, they contain "Pillagers", the opposite of Villagers which attack using Crossbows, Melee weapons and magic.

a lake or river and fish. You just need sticks and string to make a fishing rod, and your set. Cast the rod, and when bubbles start tugging the rod, click the interact button and you’ll pull in a fish. If you’re lucky, you may pull in some other stuff

MINING:
-iron ore is very good. It’s easy to find and the tools and armor it makes can be very efficient. Iron pick axe is the “weakest” material that can be used to mine diamonds

-diamonds are basically one of the best things you can find during a cave dive. They work very well.

- I would recommend you making a shield. I’m pretty sure it only requires some wood planks and only one piece of iron Ingot. When crouched, a shield can absorb multiple creeper (the green exploding things) blasts and take a lot of skeleton arrows. I play on ps4 and use the manual, so I don’t know the exact placements for a shield.

-there are 2 things like furnaces. These two are Blast furnaces and smokers. A blast furnace only smelts ores, however it does it at twice the speed. A smoker only cooks food, but again it does it at twice the speed. I don’t know the recipes for these items, so you might need to search it up.

OTHER:
- like you mentioned, you do need a saddle to ride a horse. However, a saddle can be pretty difficult to get. The only ways I know how is to either get one from fishing, find them in a dungeon chest, or from the nether. You can also get them from raids, which I’ll explain later.

- you don’t really need to know this now, but you can craft an enchanting table to enchant items to give them special perks. For example, you can make your sword be able to set things on fire. You can also make an anvil to combine your tool/armor with an enchanting book. However, both will cost XP. Those green balls you were talking about are XP points and are important if you want to enchant items.

VILLAGES:
If you explore your world enough, you may stumble upon a village. These can be very good. They villagers are passive, and if you have items or emeralds, you can trade with them. Villages have farms and are filled with goods inside of chests. If you take their stuff, they won’t mind. However, a village can have an iron golem, which is also passive unless you attack it or attack a villager. But other than that, if you find a village you can get some pretty good loot.

*FARMING - MORE FOOD*

Hey Cory, so there's another way you can get some food, and it's called farming. It takes some time, but eventually you'll get some nice good ol' fashioned bread. First, you need to make a hoe using 2 sticks and 2 wood, and you want to use it on some dirt/grass by right clicking, tilling it and preparing it for growing. Also, to make sure your food grows quick, your dirt should be right next to some water, so that it can get hydrated (darker). Now you'll need some seeds. To get some, go ahead and break some grass (not the blocks but the plants on top of them), and some may have seeds, some may not. Once you have your seeds, go ahead and plant them into your tilled ground and wait.... After you have waited, your crops will grow and grow until it turns from green into a kinda-yellow color. When it turns that color, they're ready. Break them by left clicking to get your wheat, and as a bonus you get some seeds back, so you can plant them again and continue the cycle! You need 3 wheat to make 1 piece of bread, and although it takes a while, it's fun!


Also, side note, make some fences and a gate to protect your crops. Mobs like cows and pigs and such may walk on top of your crops , ruining them, and we don't want that! So, protect your farm so that your animals don't trample them! Also, to ensure your crops grow the quickest, make sure there is water nearby, and make sure your farm is well lit (by placing torches all around). They grow quicker in light than in dark (so technically you can grow crops underground if you have torches).

*HERDING - SAVING ANIMALS*

I know you've talked about keeping the animals and not killing them too soon so that you don't run out too quick, farming allows you to do that! Let me explain:


Chickens are attracted to seeds; if you hold them in your hand, they will walk towards you. Make a small section with fences and a gate, and lead your chickens into that section. Once they are inside, quickly switch items so that they don't follow you and block them in. Once you have 2 chickens in your pen, feed both of them some seeds, and they will, well, let's just say do it. Boom! You have 3 chickens! Keep doing the same thing to grow your supply. You can do the same thing with cows and sheep, except with wheat instead of seeds. For pigs, you gotta use carrots.


P.S. If you wanna make leather armor, killing cows and horses gives you leather.
