Cory, this is info on almost every mob in the game. Feel free to correct me if I'm wrong.

*Bee* - Found in bee nests under the leaves of trees. They drop nothing when killed. Are normally passive, unless you break the nest or attack them. If they pollinate nearby flowers they will add honey to the beehive. When the honey is filled in the bee nests holes, you can right click with empty bottles to get bottles of honey (food item).
*Blaze* - Found in the nether and will spawn out of monster spawners in Nether Fortresses. They shoot fireballs and will drop blaze rods upon death, which can be used to craft blaze powder or brewing stands. They will be damaged by water or snowballs.
*Cat* - Found in villages and can be tamed with raw fish. They are tamable and will attack Creepers.
*Cave Spider* - Found in abandoned mineshafts underground and only spawn from monster spawners. They drop the normal stuff to spiders, but will poison you if they attack you.
*Chicken* - Found anywhere in the overworld above ground. They can be killed for raw chicken and feathers, but will regularly drop eggs which can be used to craft food items. They can be bred when 2 are right clicked with any type of seeds.
*Cow* - Found anywhere in the overworld above ground. Drop raw beef and leather on death. Can be bred when two are right clicked with wheat. Can be right clicked with a bucket to get bucket of milk
*Creeper* - Found in dark areas and will explode when close to a player. Can be killed for gunpowder, and if a skeleton kills one, they will drop a music disc which can be placed in a jukebox.
*Dolphin* - Found in water and oceans and will give a player "Dolphin's Grace" which speeds them up in water. Will follow diamonds and if fed, will lead the player to ruins.
*Donkey* - Found anywhere in the overworld above ground and can tamed using wheat. You can place a chest on them as mobile storage.
*Drowned* - Found under water, especially in ruins, and will drop rotten flesh, and sometimes gold on death. They will also drop the item they have in their hand, such as fishing rods and nautilus shells. If they spawn with a trident, they can be killed for a very small chance of a trident being dropped.
*Elder Guardian* - Found in ocean monuments. Will attack with a big laser similar to guardians, and will drop sponge upon death. Will also give mining fatigue if a player is too close.
*Ender Dragon* - The "Final Boss" of the game. Only found in The End and will drop tons of XP, summon a Dragon Egg, and open the end portal back to the OverWorld, upon death. Will heal using end crystals that are on giant obsidian pillars. Can be respawned using end crystals placed on the the end portal.
*EnderMan* - Found in all three dimensions and will drop ender pearls upon death. Will become hostile when looked at or attacked. They can teleport and pick up blocks and will be damaged by lava and water. Won't attack if the player wears a carved pumpkin on their head.
*Endermite* Found whenever the player throws an ender pearl and drop nothing upon death.
*Evoker* - Found in raids and Woodland mansions. Drops "Totem Of Undying" upon death which (if held) will save the player from death. Will summon Vexes and Teeth out of the ground to attack players.
*Ghast* - Found in the nether and will shoot at the player with giant fireballs that can be hit back. Will drop Ghast Tears and Gunpowder upon death.
*Guardian* - Found in ocean monuments and will attack the player with lasers out of their eyes. Will drop prismarine shards, crystals, and fish upon death.
*Horse* Found anywhere in the overworld above ground and can be tamed by riding. Can only be ridden with saddles, and can have armor put on them.
*Iron Golem* - Found in villages and can be summoned by placing four iron blocks in a T shape with a carved pumpkin on top. Will attack any hostile mobs and the player if they attack. Can be healed by right clicking with iron ingots. Will drop iron ingots and poppys upon death.
*Llama* - Found in extreme hills and can be tamed if ridden. Can have carpet placed on them as decoration. Will attack the player by spitting on them if they attack. Are also found with Wandering Traders.
*Magma Cube* - Found in the nether (especially Nether Fortresses) and when killed, will split into smaller versions. Will drop magma cream upon death.
*Mooshroom*  - Found in Mushroom Islands, and will drop raw beef upon death. Can be right clicked with bowls and will give Mushroom Stew. Can be sheared and will turn into a normal cow, dropping mushrooms.
*Panda* - Found in Bamboo Forests and cannot be tamed. Will attack if their young are attacked by the player. Drop nothing upon death.
*Parrot* Found in Jungles and can be tamed with seeds. Will die if right clicked with a cookie. Will ride the player's shoulder once tamed and will fly after the player. They can also mimic mobs nearby to warn the player, and will dance if a jukebox is playing. Will drop feathers upon death.
*Phantom* - Found whenever the player hasn't slept in a bed for 3 or more days. Will drop phantom membranes upon death, which can be used to repair elytras and brew potions of Slow Falling. Undead mob, meaning they burn in sunlight.
*Pig* - Found anywhere in the overworld above ground. Can be bred if 2 are right clicked with carrots. Will drop raw pork upon death. Can be ridden if a saddle is placed on them, and can be steered with Carrot on a Stick.
*Pillager* - Found in Patrols, Raids, and Pillager Outposts. Will attack with a crossbow and drop crossbows and emeralds upon death. Naturally hostile to players and villagers.
*Polar Bear* - Found in Glaciers. Drop fish upon death, and will attack the player if attacked, or too close to their young.
*Rabbit* - Found anywhere in the overworld above ground and drop raw rabbit, and sometimes a rabbits foot upon death. Can be bred if 2 are right clicked with carrots.
*Ravager* - Found in Raids. Will drop a saddle upon death, and can be ridden by pillagers and vindicators, but not the player.
*Sheep* - Found anywhere in the overworld above ground. Will drop wool and raw mutton upon death. When sheared they will drop 1-3 wool of their color. Can be dyed by right clicking with any dye. Can be bred by right clicking 2 with wheat.
*Shulker* - Found in end cities and will attack by shooting balls that give levitation upon hitting the player. Will drop shulker shells upon death that can be used to craft shulker boxes.
*Silverfish* Found in Strongholds and will spawn when Infested Stone is broken. Others will break when silverfish are attacked, spawning more silverfish.
*Skeleton* - Found in dark areas in the overworld, and sometimes the nether. Will attack the player with a bow. Will drop bones, arrows, and sometimes bows upon death. Undead mob, meaning they burn in sunlight unless in water or with a piece of armor on their head. Also they have aimbot.
*Slime* - Found in certain slime chunks in dark areas or swamps. Will split into smaller versions upon death, and on the last phase will drop slimeballs.
*Snow Golems* - Can be summoned by placing 2 snow blocks and a carved pumpkin stacked. Will set snow below them and the pumpkin can be sheared off. Will drop snowballs upon death.
*Spider* - Found in dark areas of the overworld. Can climb flat walls and will drop spider eyes and string upon death.
*Stray* - Found in ice spikes biomes, and will attack with a bow and arrows of slowness. Will drop arrows of slowness, bones, and sometimes a bow upon death.
*Turtle* - Found on shores and drop nothing upon death. Can be bred if 2 are right clicked with seagrass. When the young grow to adults they will drop scutes that can be crafted into a turtle shell that will grant the player 10 seconds of water breathing.
*Villager* - Found in villages and can be traded with for items. Will rush into their houses at nighttime, or when a bell is rung. Drop nothing upon death, and when attacked, their prices will drastically raise. If killed by a zombie they will become a zombie villager, and can be restored by being effected with a potion of weakness, and fed with a golden apple. When attacked, an iron golem will attack the player.
*Vindicator* - Found in patrols, raids, and woodland mansions. Will drop emeralds upon death.
*Witch* - Found in dark areas in the overworld and also witch's huts. Will attack with potions of poison, harming, and slowness, and can heal themselves with potions of healing and fire resistance. Have a chance of dropping sticks, redstone dust, glowstone dust, gunpowder, sugar, bottles, and spider eyes upon death.
*Wither* - Boss summoned by placing 4 soul sand in a T shape with 3 wither skeleton skulls on top. Will attack by throwing skulls that give the player the Wither effect. When a mob is killed by the wither, a wither rose will be placed that gives the Wither effect when walked over. Will drop a nether star upon death that can be used to craft a beacon.
*Wither Skeleton* - Found in nether fortresses and will give the player the Wither effect if they attack. Will drop bones, coal, and a small chance of a wither skeleton skull upon death.
*Wolf* - Found in forests in the overworld. Can be tamed with bones and will follow the player and attack skeletons. Will attack any mob if attacked by the player, or if they attack the player. Their collar can be dyed as well.
*Zombie* - Found anywhere in dark areas of the overworld. Will drop rotten flesh, and a small chance of dropping iron ingots, potatoes, and carrots upon death. Undead mob, meaning they burn in sunlight unless in water or with a piece of armor on their head. Also have a desert variant called "Husk"
*Zombie Pigman* - Found in the nether and will only attack the player if they attack one of them. Will drop gold nuggets and rotten flesh and small chance of gold ingots and gold swords upon death.

Tips for Cory:
-Killing the peaceful creatures you saw (besides horse and squid) will give you food
-Eating the food refills your hunger (but cooking the food first refills more hunger)
-To cook food, you need 8 cobble stone, which you can get by mining stone with a wooden pickaxe
-Having a full hunger bar will refill your health
-To craft a bed, you need wool which you can get from killing sheep
-Three wool and three wooden planks will craft a bed, which you can sleep in to pass night time, not allowing monsters to spawn
-Wooden tools are a good start, but I recommend using the wooden pickaxe to get enough stone to craft stone tools, which are much more efficient
-Your first house isn't actually a terrible start, but you will want to find someway to light it up as monsters can still spawn inside if it's too dark (and it is)
-The most basic and easy light source to obtain are torches, which are made with one stick and one coal
-Coal is found underground and can be mined using any pickaxe, but again I recommend getting a stone one first to make quicker work
-Another way to get coal is by using a furnace to cook a piece of wood, using another piece of wood, creating charcoal
-Charcoal has the same effect and cook time of regular coal
-(If you reach this part in the next episode) You may run into some iron while mining, which can only be collected with a stone pickaxe or better
-This drops iron ore, which isn't usable until you put it into a furnace to smelt it into iron ingots, which give you better tools/weapons
-For quicker crafting, hold shift and then click on the item you have crafted to gather it all at once, instead of in segments

2: You need a *pickaxe* to get better recourses. (Stone, Iron, Gold, Diamond, etc.) (Craftable with 3 Wooden Planks and 2 Sticks)
3: You are gonna need some *armor* to survive. There are 4 types of armour. Leather, (obtained by cows and horses) Iron, Gold, Diamond. (There's also Chain Armor but it's uncraftable, only obtained by dungeons.
4: When you get a pickaxe, don't mine at night, there will be monsters underground, it's best if it's safe outside.
5: Put *torches* in your house. (Craftable by 1 Stick and 1 Coal) (Coal is obtainable throught minding, duh.) If you don't put Torches inside your house, monsters will be able to spawn in there. (Mobs spawn in the dark).
6: If you don't want torches, get *windows*. You need 8 stone to make a *furnace* and then burn some sand with it. You need to get some *coal* to power up the furnace ofc. 
7: Killing animals gives you food. I reccommend you kill cows, pigs, and chicken. They offer Steak, Pork, and Raw Chicken. When Cooked all of these give a good amount of hunger back.
8: You can craft a *shield* to block all damage and the Skeleton's arrows. (Craftable with Iron and Wood, I don't remember how much exactly, sumimasen.)
9: There is a specific mob called the *Enderman.* They are tall, black figures with purple eyes. They are passive, they won't hurt you, unless you *look at them in the eyes.*
10: The Endermen drop an item which is called the *Ender Pearl.* If you throw them with right click, you will *teleport* wherever the Ender Pearl dropped.
11: If you find a pumpkin, use *Shears* to change it by right clicking it into a *Carved Pumpkin.* If you wear the Carved Pumpkin, the Endermen will *not* see you as a threat when you look at them.


*ADVANCED TIPS* (You can stop here if you want to).


1: When you obtain a Diamond pickaxe, you need to go underground and search for *obsidian.* It can be used to create a *Nether Portal,* which will help you progress.
2: You can craft an *Enchanting table* , it will give various types of buffs to your items / your armour.
3: You can craft an item called *Eye of Ender* which will lead you to the *Stronghold* where the *End* Portal is. The Eye of Ender is craftable with 1 Ender Pearl and 1 Blaze Powder (obtained by killing a Blaze in the Nether). Be Careful thought, they have a chance of breaking instead of dropping after use. You also need to craft more than one, because you will need some to activate the End Portal.
4: In the End there is a ton of Endermen, so I reccommend you go there with A: Full Diamond Armor, or B: Diamond Armor and a Carved Pumpkin.

That's all for now, please continue these series! :D

Big tips for you Cory:

*~surviving the night~*
•build a bed out of 3 wool and 3 wood to sleep during the night and avoid the monsters. This bed also sets your spawn point to where the bed is, so if you die, you will respawn safe in your house.

•if you find yourself out in the dark, make sure you have food with you.


*~mining~*
•One of the most important parts of the game is mining- to start you need to craft a wooden pickaxe(3 wood and 2 sticks)

•look for a couple of minutes around for an opening in the ground- a cave.

•begin by mining some stone, and getting a new, more powerful pickaxe

•find and mine coal ore to make torches(1 coal and 1 stick) so that you can light up the cave to see where you are going, and light up the house as well.

•using the new stone pickaxe, look for some iron ore in the cave.
•you need to smelt iron ore to make iron ingots. This can be done by making a furnace (8 cobblestone in a ring) and using coal as fuel. You can make new, more powerful and durable tools and be in a great position.


*~house~*
•the house needs to be lit with torches to prevent monsters spawning nearby and inside.

•you can make chests (8 wood in a ring) to leave your excess stuff in for when you need to travel

•you can make the house as beautiful and sophisticated as you want, but for now what you have is perfect- it'll keep you safe from monsters 


*~farming + food~*
•you need a stable source of food. This is really important to stay alive and not starve.

• you can start a farm by using a hoe on the grass, and then planting your wheat seeds you found from the grass to grow wheat.

•this wheat can be used to make bread, so you can stay at full hunger and regenerate health

•You make sheep and cows follow you by holding wheat- this means you can trap them in a pen built with fences, and make them breed together to develop a good meat source.


I know this is a lot to take in, being a minecraft noob is very daunting, but hopefully if you follow some of these tips you can take a step in the right direction :)

The message at the start says "Limited portions of the tape have been released to the public" and that's why there were time jumps. We are simply viewers of the recorded footage that has been made available to us.
The other possibility, my own personal theory:
The interview on the tape recorder was between a doctor and his female patient. Towards the end of their conversation, you can hear that the patient's voice and demeanor change completely, clearly suggesting dissociative identity disorder. People with DID can experience "lost time," i.e. when their other personality takes over. It's possible that the footage was being recorded by the very same patient in the interview, and that the abandoned hospital WAS her hq. I'm not sure you saw it with your camera, but there's a big fire at the end of the game. There was a lot of gasoline at the hospital, so the girl may have had big plans for it after all...
As for her victims, my guess is the doctor in the interview tape. There was definitely tension there. And doctors can make a lot of money, which would explain the expensive house. There is a lot we don't know even from that theory, like why the patient walked with a limp (which is why you were so slow), why the camera kept distorting sound, where the music was coming from, why the person was interested in the occult, and why they wanted to record it in the first place. We can chalk it up to evil and insanity, I guess! Maybe demons were giving her instructions, etc. essentially preying on her mental illness and using it to their advantage. What makes me the saddest is that you would think Mei would be the “horror” of the game rather than her mother what with the way she died and the guilt that drove her father to seek redemption for what he did to her (the isolation, the lies, the fights, the medical tests, the bathtub) but she wasn’t. 还愿 (Title of this game) originally means the act of fulfilling a vow. In taoism/buddhism, you have to repay for whatever you get through prayer. Usually that means performing good deeds and more charitable acts, or simply going vegetarian. But in this game we study the goddess Cigu Guanyin that the characters here worship: Cigu doesn't actually exist in the religion but Zigu does. It originates from ancient China where She, a known beauty, was taken in as a concubine but was killed by the main wife due to jealousy. She died in the lavatory hence gaining the name of Lavatory Deity. In the game, we find that Mei Shin ultimately died in the bathroom as well. And that Cigu Guanyin might not be the good deity we thought it was. The dad shows in his trip to the underworld that he is willing to sacrifice enough (His tongue, his eyes, his blood) to repay for his daughter's health. That's how devoted he is. But what about his own pride to send her for proper treatment? In the storybook that we read, we can water the tulips with blood but they won't last long; They can't handle their own weight unless we nurture it with love. It was implied that Mei Shin got well the first time after the father started spending time to fold tulips with her but he chose to believe it was his faith that cured her, neglecting her for his religion and letting her fall into sickness again.

Towards the end in the last line of the song that Mei Shin sings, it shows it actually meant 还(hai)愿 which means still willing, in "Are you still willing (to be my father)?" The daughter forgave her father and is still willing to be her daughter again. 

One reason why this game resonates so strongly with the taiwanese public is because religious scams like this and people like mentor heuh still exist in modern day taiwan and in this religion. Societies that recruit blind followers on the basis of faith, often requiring monthly contributions that don't come in small amounts. They claim to heal without needing medical treatment, depriving believers of the treatment they really need, fix behavioural issues for children and fix broken relationships amongst other things. In the recording that the father finds in Mentor Heuh's house, all her previous clients talk about their treatment. One grandmother praying for her grandson after failing his exams for two years straight. An adulterous couple praying for the man's wife to divorce him. A man shouting at her for advising them to reject medical treatment for his father which ultimately led to his early departure despite the big contributions he provides to this Guanyin. It is worth mentioning that this Cigu Guanyin that mentor Heuh endorses is actually not a good deity, which could actually bring anyone more harm than good. Of course with internet today, the society is more knowledgable now but back in the 1980s, people were largely dependent on religion and there were so many deities to pray for. As a kid who was made to watch rituals growing up, this game really hit home for me. Everything is really realistic and meticulously done, from the designs to the dates (Mei Shin's ritual ended on October 07 1987 which was on a solar eclipse so it was a very ominous date) (the dad couldn't bring meishin to Alishan because there really was a typhoon on that day), also the singing show that mei shin was in was a very real and largely popular show that existed from 1960-1990s which produced a number of the main people in the media industry today. In its pre-release ARG, the devs got fans to search for a stalked girl on Instagram who went missing but it only turned out that the stalker was Mei Shin's cousin who went into hiding after trying to investigate the girl's religious cult and as fans uncovered more, he got into trouble for doing so. Lastly, it is worth mentioning that Red Candle's small team of 12-ish people were the ones who created all of this. Props to taiwan for developing such a beautiful game! This is an amazing asian representation.

Feng Yu and his wife, a writer and actor respectively, live in an apartment with their daughter Mei Shin. They are both pretty successful in their careers, but Li Fang steps away from acting to look after her daughter and the household. 
Mei Shin begins to suffer from an illness and is taken to the doctor to diagnose it. The doctor says that she is suffering from a mental illness and severe anxiety. Her parents, though, refuse to believe that it is a mental illness and continue to believe that it’s some kind of physical ailment.
With Li Fang not working and Feng Yu’s work drying up, the family begins to struggle for money. Mei Shin’s parents begin to argue and Yu begins to pay more attention to a cult that he has become involved with, even giving them a significant amount of money.
The cult, which involves the worshipping of a god-like figure called Cigu Guanyin and is organized by a mysterious woman, insist that they can help cure Mei Shin, and Feng Yu believe them. He is deeply devoted to both the cult and his daughter, and it begins to mess with the family.

Feng Yu and Li Fang then separate. Throughout Devotion, Li Fang is presented as some kind of supernatural threat, with Yu seeing her as a threat to both his devotion and his daughter’s health. It is possible that he killed his wife, but that is not particularly clear.
Her parents’ split only makes Mei Shin’s mental health worse, however. She is clearly devoted to her parents, wanting nothing more than to impress them. She begins to become more and more unwell, though.

Then, towards the end of Devotion, as Feng Yu becomes more and more devoted to the cult, he agrees to follow a ritual that the people he’s become devoted to say will cure his daughter.
He puts Mei Shin in a bath full of alcohol for a full week and locks her in. The cult says that it will cleanse and cure her but she dies, presumably either from the alcohol or starvation/dehydration.

Feng Yu then become riddled with guilt and it’s a little unclear what he does. Maybe he cuts out his tongue as a sacrifice or sorts, or maybe he kills himself. We hear Mei Shin say “Daddy, let’s go home,” which could be to do with them both dying. It’s this end section that’s left more up to interpretation.

Right at the end, we then see a vision of Mei Shin walking through a forest. It seems as if she is free from both her mental illness and her father.

I have anxiety and I have obsessive-compulsive disorder. What people don't realise is that OCD can be "pure O", or purely obsessive, intrusive thoughts. In the segment where the father was walking through the snakes and the blood, Mei Shin says, "I'll start imagining bad things happening. I often get the feeling that I can't get enough air, then I can't sleep. I'll fear that I'll never wake up from my dreams." This is EXACTLY what it feels like to struggle with the vicious cycle that is anxiety and OCD.

I've had horrifying intrusive thoughts and imaginings that make me feel like my heart is going to explode, and while every rational part of your mind says that xyz will never happen, or that your loved one is safe, your misfiring brain will try its hardest to convince you that you're on the verge of having a heart attack, or that the reason your loved one isn't responding to a text is because they've had a horrible accident and are dead or dying in a ditch somewhere, and it spirals, and it feels like you have a cement block on your chest when you try to breathe. Sometimes, when the therapy and medication isn't enough, finding something small to take pleasure in and distract yourself with (like origami tulips) is enough to soften the all-too-sharp edges of an episode.

I empathise with Mei Shin so much. People calling you a faker, saying you're doing things for attention, family trying to cure you with prayer instead of admitting you have a mental illness, etc. This poor little girl. This game is truly the story of a tragedy.

The "guan ling rite" is actually a real thing in Chinese culture, and whats scary is, a lot of the stuff the mentor talked about (everything being dark, follow the light of lamps, don't look at anything else, chant the mantra, etc.) during the "shadow realm", I actually used to hear these stuff from my mother a lot, who believes in Budhism. Heres the brief summary of the story:
1980 they got married and moved to a new house, thus the first segment of gameplay (putting stuff in their place), the husband is a successful script writer, and the mother is an actress. They are going to have a child, but the child wasn't born yet.


1985 the child has panic attacks a lot due to stress of performing on stage and the pressure from everyone's expectations AND the growing financial problem of the family due to the father running out of good writing ideas. And the promised trip to Ali mountain which would cheer her up a lot got canceled due to a typhoon. Thus came the panic attacks. The daughter was scared of medical treatment because of all the pain, the father's heart is broken at this sight, thus he seeked out a different approach to cure his daughter (the scene where you pull out the needles), which is religion. But at the same time, he poured a lot more love into her daughter and stayed by her side more, even bought her a  story book and read it to her, which made her happy, which decreased her panic attacks and heart problems. She got better, but the father mistook that for the religion's doings, so he became devoted to the religion.


1986 the financial problem grew worse, and the family quarrel occured. The daughter heard them fighting, and also heard about part of the problem being the father spending money on the religion, which she interpreted as its her fault, which gave her a giant panic attack. And THEN the mom left the house to make money, which made the daughter's condition even worse. You see on her creative writing paper that she had to erase "My family consists of me, my father and my mother" because her mother was no longer there. All these reasons made her suffer from panic attacks even more severely then the one last year. The father, desperate, would do anything to help his daughter. Which the only thing he knew that could help is the mentor's guidance. The mentor saw his desperation and scammed him for one last time (probably won't be able to after this because the daughter would be dead and he wouldn't believe in her anymore), gave him a task that which he would be bound at home for 7 days and fled the place. So the father locked her daughter in the bathroom, soaked her in snake wine for 7 days and didn't let her out, and as the days go by he got worried and contacted the mentor, whom stopped answering his calls after some time. The seven days finally passed and he opened the bathroom door.


Now there are two interpretations here in Taiwan about this ending:
1. The daughter is fuckin dead and he sat on the couch, lost all will to live and stares blankly at the television, imagining the "Flawless Present" he wanted (the after credit scene)


2.  He opened the door and found no one there, because the mother came back once and found this horrific stuff going on and sent the daughter to the hospital, which saved her life. The father didn't know about this OR his is under custody so he stared blankly at the television on the couch reflecting on his mistakes.


Obviously the first one is more possible so that probably is the canon ending.

I myself don't have Alzheimer's, but my grandma did.. from my point of view, this is probably very accurate. It started slow with my grandma doing silly things like hiding our shoes in a tree, but it started getting noticeable by the time I was 12. She was a women's rights activist waaaayyyy back, she ran for governor of her town, she was a good journalist, she was a loyal and great wife for my grandma when he served in WW2, and she was always the liberal other half to my grandpa's strong conservative political stances. But my grandparents were so great together, man. We went on family vacations every year with them. And even when my grandma started forgetting her grandkids' names... Then her kids' names... Then her husband's name... Then her own name... My grandpa was always the best spouse he could be for her, and he made sure she had a good life even after she couldn't speak English and couldn't control her bodily waste functions. 

Alzheimer's is a terrifying disease because it just tears away your past from you, then your present, then your future. But I'm glad my grandma had a hell of a good spouse to go through it.

okay so from what I can tell, the subs are accurate so don’t worry about them. The story is (from my interpretation) a father who is haunted by his daughter’s death. She has some lung thoracic issues (which may have been caused by the drowning Cory mentioned towards the end? Or she drowned because she couldn’t sing) so she can’t sing anymore and can no longer fulfill her dreams of being a superstar like her mum (thus the static pause before she actually performs in the show). The protagonist of the game is trapped in a sort of time loop within the same setting as he explores and tries to confront the nightmare fuel-ish situations of his life. 

From marrying and moving in with his successful talented actress wife (1980), to celebrating his daughter’s bday (1986), to his daughter’s lung issue (1985). By putting all the scattered important pieces of his memory back, it’s causing him pain to recall (thus the effects). And the bday scene in particular, the piano and songbook shows her passion for music and her desire to become a famous musician/singer. The ballerina on the cake that was twisted grotesquely represents how she will never fulfill that dream of hers. Mei Shin’s doll (or you can pronounce the “Shin” as “seen” in your own accent) may be a physical representation of herself, her in surgery with all the needles.

Also the reason why the protagonist isn’t seen in all the photos is because he is ashamed of himself. In Chinese there’s a term called “丢脸” which directly translates to “lose face” meaning to be embarrassed or ashamed of oneself. So he portrays that emotion he’s feeling onto the photos he sees in his nightmare loops. As for the mum, she seems to be a bit more of a mystery at least to me so other Samurai bros and sisters feel free to share what y’all think!!

ps the man and woman in the 1986 scene look like puppets/dolls especially with the woman’s makeup. (it’s very traditional Chinese opera stage makeup) They’re not as lively or human-like even so idk it’s probably an art style to convey that some segments of the nightmare are less real than others 🤷🏻‍♀️

Fun fact! Koreans also have the same culture whereby during their kids’ 1st bday or 100 days (i forgot) they leave certain objects out for the kid to pick.

I think the final drowning scene might just be the protagonist drowning in his thoughts and grief rather than being related to the daughter as he may be trying to take his own life.

There's so many people out there like me that love Cory, and all those people are let down because their favorite YouTuber doesn't upload for weeks at a time, sometimes months. A two second video with text saying "I'll be gone for a while." Anything. I wouldn't care if you left YouTube for 5 years, just tell us when you're gonna be gone. Your channel is "dead" because you leave YouTube without saying *anything* to your audience, and leave them in the dark for sometimes MONTHS at a time. People wouldn't mind these breaks so much if you would just inform people about them. Look at YouTubers like Dashie, Markiplier, Jack, etc--they ALWAYS let people know if they're going to not be uploading. ALWAYS. 

I'm going to wrap up here. Please Cory, if you actually care about your channel and your fans, please make an effort to be consistent with your uploads, and if you can't be consistent for whatever reason (there's a lot of reasons, I know, life can be difficult for all of us), please just...update us. It doesn't have to be complicated at all. A tweet or a very short video. All people want is to know what's going on.

Step 1: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Step 3:Place the ground beef into a skillet over medium heat, add the garlic, garlic powder, oregano, salt, and black pepper to the skillet. Cook the meat, chopping it into small chunks as it cooks, until no longer pink, about 10 minutes. Drain excess grease.

Step 5:Place 4 noodles side by side into the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking pan; top with a layer of the tomato-basil sauce, a layer of ground beef mixture, and a layer of the cottage cheese mixture.
